jobs.title: Sr. Director of PR and Strategic Partnerships
jobs.description:
Established in 1985, The ALS Association is the only national nonprofit organization fighting ALS on every front. By leading the way in global research, providing assistance for people with ALS through a nationwide network of chapters, coordinating multidisciplinary care through certified clinical care centers, and fostering government partnerships, the Association builds hope and enhances quality of life while aggressively searching for new treatments and a cure

Position Summary
The Sr. Director of PR and Strategic Partnerships provides strategic leadership in elevating the ALS Association’s brand, expanding its influence, and strengthening its reputation through high-impact public relations initiatives and strategic partnerships. This role focuses on building relationships with organizations, institutions, businesses, and influential stakeholders that extend the Association’s reach, increase awareness of its mission, and reinforce its position as a leading voice in the ALS community.

Public relations and strategic partnerships are viewed as core organizational functions that drive brand visibility, strengthen stakeholder trust, identify new opportunities for collaboration, and inform organizational decision-making. The Sr. Director will develop and execute integrated strategies that leverage partnerships to elevate the ALS Association’s brand, amplify its mission, increase engagement, and advance its long-term priorities.
Working closely with executive leadership and cross-functional teams, this individual will identify and cultivate partnerships that create meaningful value for the Association, its supporters, and the ALS community while advancing the mission to make ALS a livable disease while working toward a world without ALS.

Strategic Public Relations and Brand Elevation
  • Develop and execute integrated public relations and brand strategies that strengthen the ALS Association’s reputation, visibility, credibility, and influence.
  • Establish strategic partnerships as a key driver of brand awareness, audience growth, community engagement, and organizational impact.
  • Identify opportunities to align the ALS Association with mission-compatible organizations, institutions, businesses, and influential stakeholders to expand its reach and strengthen brand recognition.
  • Build a consistent and compelling public presence that reinforces the Association’s leadership, impact, and commitment to the ALS community.
  • Identify emerging reputational, political, regulatory, and community issues that may affect the Association and recommend proactive strategies.
  • Ensure public relations and partnership initiatives align with organizational priorities, programmatic goals, fundraising objectives, and long-term brand strategy.

Community Engagement and Strategic Partnerships
  • Develop and execute a strategic partnership approach that elevates the ALS Association’s brand and expands its presence across relevant industries, communities, and stakeholder networks.
  • Identify, cultivate, and manage partnerships that increase awareness of ALS, introduce the Association to new audiences, and create opportunities for deeper engagement.
  • Build relationships with healthcare organizations, corporations, advocacy groups, community organizations, and other mission-aligned partners to advance shared objectives.
  • Create collaborative opportunities that leverage partner platforms, resources, expertise, and networks to amplify the Association’s mission and programs.
  • Work cross-functionally to develop partnership initiatives that deliver measurable value, strengthen brand affinity, and support organizational priorities.
  • Ensure partnerships reflect the Association’s values and contribute meaningfully to its reputation, visibility, and impact.
Program and Mission Public Relations
  • Lead public relations strategies that increase awareness and understanding of the Association’s programs, services, initiatives, and impact.
  • Partner with program leaders and cross-functional teams to identify compelling stories, outcomes, and opportunities that demonstrate the value of the Association’s work.
  • Leverage strategic partnerships to amplify program visibility, support launches and expansions, and increase engagement with key initiatives.
  • Develop collaborative opportunities that connect the Association’s programs with external partners, platforms, and audiences to broaden reach and strengthen mission awareness.
  • Translate complex programmatic information into accessible, engaging narratives that resonate with people living with ALS, families, healthcare professionals, partners, donors, and the broader public.
  • Ensure program public relations efforts reinforce the Association’s brand and demonstrate how its work supports people living with ALS and their families.
Executive Counsel and Issues Management
  • Serve as a trusted advisor to executive leadership on brand strategy, public relations, partnership opportunities, stakeholder perceptions, and reputational considerations.
  • Provide strategic guidance on partnership decisions and external opportunities that may affect the Association’s brand, credibility, or mission.
  • Identify emerging opportunities to strengthen the Association’s influence, expand its network, and elevate its position within the nonprofit, healthcare, advocacy, and corporate sectors.
  • Anticipate potential challenges and develop proactive strategies to address issues affecting the organization, its programs, partnerships, or the ALS community.
  • Bring external perspectives and stakeholder insights into strategic discussions and organizational planning.
Qualifications
  • Bachelor’s degree in public relations, communications, marketing, business, public affairs, or a related field required; advanced degree preferred.
  • Seven to ten years of progressive experience in public relations, brand strategy, strategic partnerships, business development, or a related field, including senior-level leadership experience.
  • Demonstrated success developing strategies that elevate organizational brands, expand visibility, and strengthen reputation through strategic partnerships.
  • Experience cultivating relationships with corporate, healthcare, nonprofit, advocacy, and other mission-aligned partners.
  • Proven ability to identify and execute partnerships that create shared value, expand audience reach, and advance organizational objectives.
  • Experience advising executive leadership and navigating sensitive issues, complex stakeholder relationships, and reputational risks.
  • Strong strategic judgment, relationship-building skills, written and verbal communication abilities, and cross-functional leadership experience.
  • Experience in nonprofit, healthcare, advocacy, or association environments preferred.
  • A demonstrated commitment to the mission of the ALS Association and the needs of people living with ALS and their families.
Measures of Success
  • Increased recognition, visibility, and positive perception of the ALS Association’s brand.
  • Strategic partnerships that expand the Association’s reach, introduce new audiences to its mission, and strengthen its position as a leading voice in the ALS community.
  • Measurable growth in partner engagement, collaborative initiatives, and opportunities for shared impact.
  • Increased awareness and understanding of the Association’s programs, services, and mission.
  • Stronger stakeholder trust and relationships across the ALS community and key partner networks.
  • Effective integration of public relations and strategic partnerships into organizational planning and priorities.
  • Proactive management of reputational risks and identification of opportunities to strengthen the Association’s influence and brand.
PAY TRANSPARENCY:
The ALS Association’s pay range for this position is $110,000–$125,000 annually.

The ALS Association has compensation ranges for various work locations throughout the United States, allowing us to compensate employees competitively and consistently in diverse geographic markets. The above-listed listed range shows prospective compensation for this role; the appropriate range will be established by what is eventually determined to be the candidate's primary work location. Various factors, including the complexity and significance of the role, job duties/requirements, relevant experience and abilities, and primary work location, determine individual compensation. Compensation ranges are evaluated and typically adjusted on a regular basis. Offers are made within the compensation range that is in effect at the time of the job offer.

The Association may, at its discretion, offer merit-based increases tied to individual performance. The benefits listed may differ depending on employment status with the Association. Healthcare benefits, a 401(k) plan with employer match, short-term and long-term disability coverage, basic life insurance, well-being benefits, paid time off and several paid holidays are available to Association employees, among other benefits.

We are an equal opportunity employer, and all qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, pregnancy, age, national origin, disability status, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

jobs.description:
Shape a SAP architecture designed to scale with InPost

We are looking for an experienced SAP Solution Architect (m/f/n) to take architectural ownership of InPost Group's evolving SAP ecosystem, spanning integration and middleware, systems roadmaps, and the global SAP S/4HANA template.

This is an opportunity to influence technology decisions across a fast-growing international organization. You will connect business priorities, technology capabilities and architectural principles to create a SAP landscape that remains coherent, scalable and maintainable as the organization evolves.

Where you will make an impact

Create a coherent integration architecture

You will shape how SAP connects to InPost's critical business systems, including WMS, TMS, EAM/PAM, InvoiceAggregator, Paycom, Pascom, CRM and billing platforms.

You will:

  • define integration standards based on SAP BTP, Integration Suite, API Management and Event Mesh,
  • establish and evolve the API catalogue, versioning policies and lifecycle management,
  • select appropriate integration patterns across APIs, ESB, event-driven architectures and iPaaS,
  • review integration designs and partner with delivery teams during implementation,
  • establish standards covering REST, OData, SOAP, EDI, RFC/BAPI, IDoc and gRPC.

A central part of your role will be shaping and governing the global SAP S/4HANA system template.

You will establish clear principles around clean core, standard functionality and extension boundaries, while building reusable integration and extension patterns for country rollouts.

Across Poland, Italy, Iberia and Luxembourg, you will evaluate local requirements and help determine whether capabilities belong in the global core or should remain local extensions.

You will thrive in this role if you:

  • have 7+ years of SAP experience, including at least 3 years as an architect or senior technical consultant,
  • have strong hands-on understanding of SAP S/4HANA architecture, clean core and extensibility,
  • know SAP BTP, especially Integration Suite (CPI/iFlow), API Management, Event Mesh and BAS,
  • understand ABAP Cloud, RAP and CAP,
  • are comfortable working with REST, SOAP, OData, EDI, RFC/BAPI, IDoc and gRPC,
  • understand OpenAPI/Swagger, AsyncAPI and BPMN,
  • have enough functional knowledge of FI/CO, SD, MM, WM/EWM and TM to assess architectural implications,
  • are familiar with TOGAF, SAP EA Framework or an equivalent architecture framework,
  • can communicate architecture through C4, sequence and landscape diagrams,
  • understand Domain-Driven Design and microservices architecture,
  • understand integration security, including OAuth2, SAML, mTLS and encryption in transit and at rest.

What we offer

  • Fulfilling careers with a range of benefits for people and investing in providing training opportunities for their development.
  • You will feel a part of the InPost community that makes an impact on sustainability, convenient deliveries, and the circular economy every day.
  • Excellent environment and flexible hours
  • We offer B2B type of contract

InPost Group is an innovative European out of home deliveries company, revolutionizing the way parcels are delivered to customers. With operations across several countries, our network of intelligent lockers provides customers with a fast, convenient, and secure delivery option. InPost Group is a publicly traded company, with a market capitalization of about $5 billion as of March 2023. With over 10,000 people worldwide, InPost Group is one of the largest out of home delivery providers in Europe, committed to providing sustainable and efficient delivery solutions to meet the evolving needs of customers in today's rapidly changing landscape.

jobs.title: Director of HR Operations
jobs.description:
Geode Health is a rapidly growing, national provider of outpatient mental health services. Our Mission is to “Transform mental health by making it more accessible, affordable and effective”.

About the role

The Director of HR Operations owns the systems, analytics, compensation programs, and compliance processes that keep our people function running accurately and at scale. In our outpatient behavioral healthcare setting, that means supporting providers, clinical teams and corporate staff across multiple states, and the business-aligned HR processes that help the People team function as productive, collaborative partners to the business.

This leader oversees HR Systems, project manager, compliance, and analytics and compensation. They partner closely with HR Business Partners, Finance, Legal, Compliance, Credentialing, IT and operational leaders to turn HR strategy into reliable, efficient, and business aligned programs.

This leader is both strategist and hands-on contributor. They set direction for compensation, payroll and HR compliance, and they also build the models, run the analysis and deliver the cycles themselves, in close partnership with Finance.

Reports to: Chief People Officer

Direct reports: HRIS Manager/Team; HR Operations Analyst

Key responsibilities

HR Systems

  • Own the HR systems ecosystem end to end, including core HR functions; hiring, compensation, performance management, absence, time tracking, payroll integrations, recruiting and related modules.
  • Partner with the Workday Manager to configure, test and manage system updates, including feature releases,with documented testing and sign-off for changes that affect pay or compliance.
  • Partner with Workday Manager to design business processes, security roles and data governance to protect data, in line with HIPAA and internal privacy standards.
  • Oversee integrations with payroll, benefits carriers, credentialing, scheduling and timekeeping systems used by staff and clinical teams.
  • Ensure time tracking and pay rules are configured to meet state wage and hour requirements, including overtime, meal and rest breaks, and PTO accrual rules.
  • Manage vendor and implementation partner relationships, including contracts, SLAs and roadmap planning.

Compensation and Performance Management

  • Partner with Finance and executive leadership on compensation strategy, and lead compensation insights for clinical teams and corporate staff, including base pay, productivity, incentive and bonus plans.
  • Partner with Finance to model plan costs, set compensation budgets and forecast labor spend, so pay decisions are tied to the financial plan.
  • Own the salary structures, pay ranges and job architecture (job families, levels and titles), and the job evaluation approach for new and changing roles.
  • Lead and run the full calendar of performance and compensation cycles, working with Finance on budgets, accruals and payout reconciliation, including:
  • Annual performance reviews, calibration and staff merit and market adjustments
  • Monthly or quarterly team incentive and productivity payouts
  • Twice-yearly provider compensation reviews
  • Bonus, retention, one-time, and recurring programs as needed
  • Partner with Payroll and Finance so payouts are accurate, on time and correctly accounted for; oversee program documentation, administration, reporting and audits.
  • Set the standard for plan documents, program guides, manager training and pay communications - oversee the compensation support model, using trends in questions and discrepancies to improve guides, training and plan design.

HR Compliance and Controls

  • Ensure compensation packages and structures are fair, consistent, and compliant with all applicable laws and statutes, including pay transparency.
  • Own FLSA classification for all roles, including exempt and non-exempt determinations and run periodic classification audits as roles and state salary thresholds change.
  • Maintain internal controls across HR systems and payroll, including segregation of duties, approval workflows, audit trails, and support internal and external audits, agency inquiries and accreditation surveys.
  • Partner with Finance and Payroll to support accurate, timely, and compliant payroll and payroll processes, controls, and audits across all pay groups and states.

HR Analytics and Reporting

  • Own HR reporting and analytics, covering headcount, turnover, retention, time-to-fill, labor cost and provider productivity.
  • Lead the build, maintenance and refresh of workforce dashboards and recurring reports for executive and operational leaders.
  • Act as the senior HR data liaison: set metric definitions and data quality standards in HR systems, and manage intake for ad hoc data requests across the business.
  • Own regulatory and accreditation reporting, including EEO-1, state pay data reports, ACA reporting and any workforce requirements of any accrediting group.
  • Serve as the main liaison between Operations, HR and Finance on compensation, workforce planning and position management.

HR Project Management

  • Lead the HR project portfolio, including intake, prioritization, timelines, resourcing and status reporting; own compensation, compliance, payroll, analytics and systems projects from start to finish.
  • Coordinate stakeholders across Operations, Finance, Legal, IT and HR, and keep leaders informed on progress and risks.
  • Apply change management practices so new processes and tools are adopted across provider, clinical and corporate teams.
  • Drive continuous improvement and documented standard operating procedures across HR operations and payroll.

Qualifications

Required

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in HR operations, HRIS, compensation or payroll, including 5+ years leading teams in a combined HR operations leadership role.
  • Hands-on Workday HCM experience, including configuration, business processes, security and reporting.
  • Hands-on experience designing, modeling and running compensation programs, including salary structures, annual merit cycles and productivity or incentive plans, in close partnership with Finance.
  • Working knowledge of FLSA, multi-state wage and hour law, pay equity and pay transparency requirements, ACA employer reporting and data privacy requirements, including HIPAA.
  • Experience designing and maintaining internal controls and supporting internal or external audits.
  • Strong analytical skills and experience building workforce reporting and dashboards.
  • Proven track record leading complex, cross-functional HR projects from planning through adoption.
  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business, Finance, Information Systems or a related field, or equivalent experience.

Mission – Why we exist, what we do, and why we need you

SpotMe is a leading B2B event platform that helps enterprises increase the impact of their events by delivering CRM-connected, high-quality experiences across in-person, virtual, hybrid events, and webinars. With a strong focus on life sciences, SpotMe powers Onomi: an HCP engagement product that enables medical and commercial teams to run impactful congresses, symposia, advisory boards, and webinars. Together, SpotMe and Onomi turn events into a company’s most effective engagement channel.

This position is the ideal role for a legal professional who wants to make a direct impact on business operations. You'll establish and own critical processes that directly affect our bottom line and business efficiency. You'll develop your legal and commercial skills while building systems that scale with our company.

As a Legal Counsel & Procurement Manager, you will be reporting to the CFO and you will split your time between:

  • Commercial legal support (40%): Reviewing MSAs and SOWs for the deal desk, redlining third-party contracts, standardizing our commercial terms, ensuring legal compliance in sales documents, and supporting the closing process in timely manner
  • Procurement and vendor management (20%): Support the business with new vendor and vendor evaluations, leading contract negotiations, managing renewal timelines, and optimizing pricing
  • Non-commercial legal (20%): Managing employment agreements, contractor agreements, NDAs, and other internal legal documents
  • Scaling legal and procurement systems (20%): Maintaining our contract management system, building a legal request ticketing system, automating repetitive work with AI, creating standardized workflows and developing procurement policies

You will work with the Paralegal, who reports to you, and serve as the key point of contact for compliance matters with both internal teams and external stakeholders.

"Bring order to contracts, save money on vendors, and close deals faster" will be your motto.

Objectives - The problems you will solve

In your first month, you will:

  • Review our current commercial T&Cs and identify areas for standardization and simplification
  • Shadow the deal desk to understand their workflow and pain points related to MSAs and SOWs
  • Get up to speed on our contract management system and review all renewals due in the next 6 months, identifying immediate cost-saving opportunities

After 3 months, you will:

  • Launch a legal request intake (ticketing) system: one front door for all legal and procurement requests, with triage, assignment to the right owner and status tracking
  • Create standardized templates for common commercial agreements and negotiation silver bullets (for most frequently negotiated items) that reduce redlining time
  • Formalize our vendor evaluation and selection process, building on current practices

After 12 months, you will:

  • Reduce our procurement (software, services) costs by at least 10% through strategic negotiation and vendor consolidation, with specific targets of 5% on renewals and 20% on new acquisitions
  • Process 80% of commercial agreements within the same business day of receipt
  • Have trained and coached the Paralegal so she handles standard commercial requests autonomously
  • Run our contract repository proactively: 100% of renewals flagged at least 90 days ahead and renegotiated before notice deadlines
  • Handle at least 50% of standard requests (NDAs, standard DPAs, routine vendor reviews) through self-service or AI-assisted workflows

What you need to be great at:

  • Commercial contract expertise: you negotiate MSAs, SOWs and DPAs pragmatically, knowing which points to hold and which to concede.
  • Negotiation and vendor management: you get better prices and terms from vendors, and have the numbers to prove it.
  • Speed with judgement: you balance thoroughness with sales velocity and help deals close faster, not slower.
  • Structure and ownership: you build processes and systems, such as templates, playbooks and request tracking, and own them end to end.
  • Automation and AI-first mindset: you look at every manual task and ask whether it needs to be manual. You use workflows, templates and AI assistants such as Claude every day (first-pass contract review against our playbook, drafting redlines, comparing clauses, summarizing vendor terms, answering routine legal questions), and you turn them into repeatable tools the business can use on its own, such as self-service NDAs or a contract Q&A assistant, while keeping human judgement where it matters.

What we are most curious about:

  • Tell us about a time you sped up contract turnaround in a sales-driven company. What changed, and what were the numbers?
  • What's the biggest saving you've negotiated with a vendor, and how did you get there?
  • Which legal or procurement task have you automated or handed to AI, and what did it free up?
  • How do you decide what to handle yourself, what to delegate to a paralegal, and what to send to external counsel?

Who we are

Samsara (NYSE: IOT) is the pioneer of the Connected Operations™ Cloud, which is a platform that enables organizations that depend on physical operations to harness Internet of Things (IoT) data to develop actionable insights and improve their operations. At Samsara, we are helping improve the safety, efficiency and sustainability of the physical operations that power our global economy. Representing more than 40% of global GDP, these industries are the infrastructure of our planet, including agriculture, construction, field services, transportation, and manufacturing — and we are excited to help digitally transform their operations at scale.

Working at Samsara means you’ll help define the future of physical operations and be on a team that’s shaping an exciting array of product solutions, including Video-Based Safety, Vehicle Telematics, Apps and Driver Workflows, and Equipment Monitoring. As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.

About the role

Samsara is building its Federal business, and we're looking for the Sales leader who will build out the team and strategy. As the AVP of Federal Sales, you will be the first and most senior specialized Federal hire, accountable for taking the Samsara Connected Operations Cloud into U.S. federal civilian agencies as part of Phase 1 and defense agencies as part of Phase 2 on a dedicated, FedRAMP-authorized government cloud environment.

Federal agencies run some of the largest vehicle and asset fleets in the world, and they are modernizing how they manage safety, maintenance, sustainability, and mission readiness. Samsara already partners with state and local government agencies across the country, including statewide programs. This role turns that foundation into a durable federal practice.

You will operate as the leader of a dedicated federal practice: you'll design the team, hire it, set the go-to-market strategy, shape our partner and contract-vehicle approach, and own federal bookings. You'll work hand in hand with Product, Security and Compliance, Legal, Marketing, Partnerships, and Revenue Operations to make Samsara easy for federal agencies to buy and trust. This role reports to the Vice President of Public Sector Sales.

This is a remote position open to candidates based on the East Coast (Maine, New Hampshire, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, Delaware, Maryland, Pennsylvania, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, and Florida), with a preference for candidates based in the Washington D.C. metropolitan area. This position requires travel up to 40% of the time.

In this role, you will:

  • Build and own Samsara's federal go-to-market strategy for civilian agencies, including agency prioritization, territory design, and a multi-year plan that sequences investment against certification milestones and the federal budget cycle - with a plan to expand to defense agencies in the future
  • Build Samsara's federal route-to-market with Partnerships: distributors and resellers, contract vehicles such as GSA MAS and GWACs, and co-sell relationships with federal systems integrators

  • Partner with Security and Compliance and Product to translate FedRAMP authorization progress into a clear, accurate customer narrative and to bring agency requirements back into the GovCloud roadmap
  • Work with Revenue Operations, Finance, and Sales Compensation to design federal-specific pipeline stages, forecasting, quotas, and compensation plans for long-cycle selling
  • Partner with Legal, Deal Desk, and Contracts on FAR-compliant terms, teaming agreements, and federal ethics requirements, setting a high bar for compliance across the team
  • Champion, role model, and embed Samsara’s cultural principles (Focus on Customer Success, Build for the Long Term, Adopt a Growth Mindset, Be Inclusive, Win as a Team) as we scale globally and across new offices

Minimum requirements for the role:

  • 12+ years of enterprise technology sales experience, with 8+ years selling to U.S. federal government agencies
  • 5+ years leading federal sales teams, including leaders of account executives, as a second-line manager or above
  • Track record of building or scaling a federal sales practice at a commercial-first SaaS, cloud, or IoT company, including selling through and after FedRAMP authorization
  • Consistent over-achievement of federal bookings targets, with closed multi-year, seven-figure agency contracts
  • Hands-on experience with federal acquisition: GSA Schedule and other contract vehicles, distributor and reseller models, and teaming with federal systems integrators
  • Established relationships with federal civilian agency stakeholders, systems integrators, and the federal partner ecosystem
  • Experience leading business development and capture for competitive federal procurements, from pre-RFP shaping through proposal and award
  • Eligibility to obtain a Public Trust position

An ideal candidate also has:

  • A network that includes experienced federal sellers, capture managers, and solutions engineers who would follow them to a new practice
  • Experience co-selling with federal systems integrators inside a direct sales organization, including clear account ownership and compensation rules
  • Familiarity with Shipley or a comparable capture and proposal methodology
  • Experience designing activity-based or MBO compensation for federal teams before authorized product is available
  • Working knowledge of FedRAMP, FAR/DFARS, Section 508 accessibility, and Buy American and Trade Agreements Act requirements, and how they show up in deals
  • Experience with Department of Defense or National Guard fleet programs, as a foundation for future expansion

jobs.title: Media Buying Manager
jobs.description:
FP Markets is a multi-regulated online CFD and forex broker with entities regulated by ASIC, CySEC, FSCA, CMA, FSA Seychelles and others. We serve traders around the world across forex, indices, commodities, shares and crypto CFDs. The Growth Team owns global client acquisition. It is managed by budget and objectives: impressions, sessions, leads, direct FTDs (first-time depositors) and maximum CPA. It is made up of the Global Paid Growth, Global Organic Growth and Regional Growth teams, supported by our Data Engineering department for reporting and insight.

The role

You will own FP Markets' direct media buying with financial media sites and broker review/comparison platforms worldwide. You will manage 30+ partner websites today and grow that list, turning every placement, listing and broker profile into measurable sessions, leads and FTDs within budget and CPA targets. This is a hands-on role for someone early in their career who is organised, works hard, takes direction well and wants to grow inside a fast-moving global marketing team.

Key responsibilities:

Partner and media management

• Manage day-to-day relationships with 30+ financial media sites, broker review and comparison platforms

• Negotiate and book direct media: banners, sponsored content, featured listings, newsletters, CPC/CPA/CPM and fixed-fee deals

• Keep FP Markets' broker profiles accurate and up to date (spreads, fees, platforms, regulation, awards) across every partner site

• Source, evaluate and onboard new media partners and broker-review sites to grow the portfolio

Campaign execution

• Plan and launch campaigns by region and regulatory entity, following the country whitelist and compliance rules

• Brief the Creative and Content teams on banners, landing pages and advertorials, and get assets approved on time

• Set up tracking links and UTMs for every placement so results can be attributed

Budget and performance

• Manage the direct media budget and track spend against plan by partner, month and region

• Report weekly and monthly on impressions, sessions, leads, FTDs, CPA and ROI per partner, with

Data

• Optimise or cut underperforming placements and scale those that deliver

• Reconcile invoices and insertion orders with Finance

Team and process

• Keep partner contracts, IOs, rates, live placements and renewal dates in a central tracker

• Manage tasks in Jira and document processes in Confluence

• Work closely with the rest of the Growth Team and support wider marketing initiatives as needed

Candidate Profile:

• 1–3 years' experience in media buying, digital marketing, affiliate or partner marketing

• Bachelor's degree in Marketing, Business, Economics or a related field

• Comfortable with numbers: tracking spend, CPA and ROI in Excel or Google Sheets

• Strong written and spoken English

• Good understanding of tracking links, UTMs and Google Analytics (GA4)

Nice to have

• Experience in online trading, forex/CFDs, fintech, crypto or iGaming

• Familiarity with the partner sites listed above

• Experience with Jira, Confluence, Salesforce or HubSpot

• A second language (e.g. Greek, Spanish, Portuguese, Arabic, Chinese)

• Awareness of financial marketing regulation (ASIC, CySEC, FSCA)

Our offer

  • A welcoming, young and multicultural team with approachable leadership.
  • Real autonomy over a large growth budget, and the chance to contribute to a dynamic business in a growth phase.
  • Support for your ideas and room to put your expertise into the company's best practices.
  • Continuous personal development, a training and development budget, growth with the company and the opportunity to learn from industry leaders.
  • Competitive remuneration, regular salary reviews and performance-based incentive schemes.
  • A vibrant company life: from team activities to global celebrations.

Journey to FP Markets

  1. Interview with HR
  2. Interview with the CMO
  3. Interview with the stakeholders

Join our team and be a part of a professional, rapidly-growing company operating in a multicultural environment!

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Regional Alliances (Northwest)
jobs.description:
GuidePoint Security provides trusted cybersecurity expertise, solutions and services that help organizations make better decisions and minimize risk. By taking a three-tiered, holistic approach for evaluating security posture and ecosystems, GuidePoint enables some of the nation’s top organizations, such as Fortune 500 companies and U.S. government agencies, to identify threats, optimize resources and integrate best-fit solutions that mitigate risk.

GuidePoint is seeking a Senior Manager, Regional Alliances for the Northwest territory to join their rapidly expanding team. In this role, you will have the opportunity to join GuidePoint at a time of unprecedented growth and make an impact by working directly with our most strategic partnerships within the Northwest region. You’ll dedicate your time to owning and executing our vision to become the fastest-growing cybersecurity solutions and services company in the US. As a key team member, you will be relied upon to elevate our partnerships with some of the most reputable security companies in the world. Working closely with their senior executives, you will ensure that internal and external stakeholders are aligned on our joint go-to-market (GTM) strategy and effectively communicate progress.

This role will report directly to the Director of Regional Alliances within the Vendor Relationship Management (VRM) department, while also maintaining a dotted-line connection to our Northwest VP of Sales and regional Sales leadership. The position will primarily collaborate with the Northwest leadership team on go-to-market strategies, while also partnering with VRM leadership for enablement, alignment, vendor insights, and escalation support.

Roles and Responsibilities:

  • Be a key contributor in architecting and executing joint go-to-market plans with high-level, business-impacting focus partnerships, specifically within the Northwest territory.
  • Lead day-to-day engagement and relationship-building with executives at our high-impact partners across the Northwest.
  • Assist in shaping the utilization of current systems, processes, KPIs, etc., and be an integral part of evolving how partnerships are measured and expanded upon within the region.
  • Collaborate with GuidePoint’s Regional Leaders on the GuidePoint and Vendor side to align key leadership and tailor a GTM strategy that addresses the unique business needs of the Northwest territory, driving KPIs with the agreed-upon Strategic Vendors.
  • Ensure all key executives of partner GTM teams are interlocked with GuidePoint at the Northwest field level.
  • Consistently communicate strategy and progress against KPIs to internal and external stakeholders, focusing on Northwest-specific metrics and growth.
  • Drive value by increasing margins and overall marketing spending, driving sales and pipeline, and enhancing partner satisfaction scores within the territory.
  • Partner with GuidePoint sales and marketing to measure results from marketing events and sales, to influence decisions on vendor participation at future marketing events
  • Lead Northwest vendor meetings while tracking & organizing vendor growth and mutual sales, along with vendor partner programs and competitive advantages
  • Tracking vendor escalations from origin to resolution, and communicating updates throughout

Experience Requirements:

  • 7-10 years of managing and accelerating large, strategic partnerships
  • Strong presentation and organizational skills are essential, along with a proven ability to communicate effectively with and coordinate with executive-level audiences (SVP/EVP, C-suite).
  • Experience working on both sides of the partnership — partner AND vendor — to bring multiple perspectives (preferred).
  • Demonstrated track record of setting and exceeding KPIs that significantly impact organizational goals.
  • Demonstrates a willingness to learn and use AI-enabled tools
  • A dynamic leader who thrives in a fast-paced environment and contributes to a ‘team-first’ culture.
  • Proven experience building and scaling a Partner Program at a cybersecurity or cloud hyper-growth startup AND/OR F1000 organization from the ground up (preferred).

We use Greenhouse Software as our applicant tracking system and Zoom Scheduler for HR screen request scheduling. At times, your email may block our communication with you. Please be sure to check your SPAM folder so that you don't miss updates on your application.

Why GuidePoint?

GuidePoint Security is a rapidly growing, profitable, privately-held value added reseller that focuses exclusively on Information Security. Since its inception in 2011, GuidePoint has grown to over 1,300 employees, established strategic partnerships with leading security vendors, and serves as a trusted advisor to more than 6,200 customers.

Firmly-defined core values drive all aspects of the business, which have been paramount to the company’s success and establishment of an enjoyable workplace atmosphere. At GuidePoint, your colleagues are knowledgeable, skilled, and experienced and will seek to collaborate and provide mentorship and guidance at every opportunity.

This is a unique and rare opportunity to grow your career along with one of the fastest growing companies in the nation.

Some added perks….

  • Remote workforce primarily (U.S. based only, some travel may be required for certain positions, working on-site may be required for Federal positions)
  • Group Medical Insurance options: Zero Deductible PPO Plan (GuidePoint pays 90% of the premium for employees and 70% for family plans (spouse/children/family) or High Deductible Health Plan with HSA (GuidePoint pays 100% of the employees premiums and 75% for family plans (spouse/children/family). If you choose the High Deductible / HSA plan, GPS will contribute in 4 equal quarterly installments: ($850 per EE annually / $1750 per family annually (includes spouse/children/family options)
  • Group Dental Insurance: GuidePoint pays 100% of the premium for employees and 75% of family plans
  • 12 corporate holidays and a Flexible Time Off (FTO) program
  • Healthy mobile phone and home internet allowance
  • Eligibility for retirement plan after 2 months at open enrollment
  • Pet Benefit Option

jobs.title: SAP Consultant
jobs.description:
Tiger Analytics is an advanced analytics consulting firm. We are the trusted analytics partner for several Fortune 100 companies, enabling them to generate business value from data. Our consultants bring deep expertise in Data Science, Data Analytics, Data Engineering, Business Intelligence, Machine Learning, and AI. Our business value and leadership have been recognized by various market research firms, including Forrester and Gartner.

We are looking for an SAP Business AI Architect to design and deliver AI-driven capabilities across the SAP landscape of our clients. You will turn business priorities into practical AI solutions built on SAP Business Technology Platform (BTP) and SAP Business Data Cloud (BDC), using governed business data as the foundation for analytics and AI.

Responsibilities

  • Define the target-state architecture and roadmap for AI and data across the SAP landscape, with BTP as the application and integration platform and BDC as the strategic data foundation.
  • Identify and prioritize high-value AI use cases with business leaders, backed by clear value cases.
  • Establish reference architectures, standards, and governance for AI, generative AI, and agentic solutions.
  • Lead data product strategy: define, publish, and govern SAP and custom data products in BDC for reuse across analytics and AI.
  • Architect AI solutions on BTP using SAP Joule, AI Core, AI Launchpad, Generative AI Hub, SAP Build, Integration Suite, and HANA Cloud (vector engine).
  • Design BDC architectures spanning SAP Datasphere, SAP Analytics Cloud, SAP HANA Cloud, and SAP Databricks, including zero-copy data sharing with Databricks and other external platforms.
  • Partner with SAP, system integrators, and hyperscalers on solution fit and roadmap alignment.
  • Design RAG, copilot, and autonomous-agent solutions that combine BTP services with governed BDC data and SAP business context.
  • Integrate third-party, open-source, and hyperscaler models (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud) with SAP systems.
  • Apply clean-core principles, using APIs, events, and ABAP Cloud/CAP on BTP for extensibility.
  • Provide technical leadership through build, deployment, and ongoing model monitoring and cost control (MLOps/LLMOps).

Required Qualifications

  • 10+ years in enterprise or solution architecture, including 5+ years in SAP environments (S/4HANA, BTP).
  • Hands-on experience designing and delivering solutions on SAP BTP, including integration, extensibility, and security.
  • Extensive knowledge of SAP BDC, Datasphere, and SAP Analytics Cloud, including data products, data modeling, and federation.
  • Hands-on experience delivering AI/ML or generative AI solutions in an enterprise setting.
  • Experience with Databricks or comparable lakehouse platforms, modern data pipelines, data governance, lineage, and master data.
  • Strong understanding of LLMs, embeddings, vector databases, RAG, and agent frameworks.
  • Excellent communication skills, with the ability to engage both technical and executive audiences.

Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Business Administration, or a related field.
  • Minimum of 5 years of experience in SAP consulting, implementation, or support.
  • Good understanding of SAP applications, modules, and business processes.
  • Experience working on SAP implementation, configuration, enhancement, and support projects.
  • Ability to understand business requirements and translate them into SAP solutions.
  • Experience working with cross-functional teams and client stakeholders.
  • Knowledge of SAP integration, testing, and troubleshooting.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently as well as in a team environment.
  • Good client-facing and stakeholder management skills.

Benefits

  • Competitive salary and comprehensive benefits package.
  • Opportunity to work on diverse SAP projects across industries.
  • Exposure to enterprise-level technology solutions and business transformation initiatives.
  • Professional development and learning opportunities.
  • Collaborative and supportive work environment.
  • Flexible work arrangements.

Experience supporting multiple businesses or QuickBooks company files. Experience with Salesforce or other CRM and case management systems. Experience collaborating with Sales, Consulting, Implementation, or other customer-facing teams.

Who We're Looking For We're not simply looking for someone who knows how to use QuickBooks. We're looking for someone who enjoys figuring out why something isn't working and how to fix it. jobs.title: Director, Site Reliability Engineering
jobs.description:
8x8 connects our customers and teams globally, empowering CX leaders with performance and insights to make smarter decisions, delight customers, and drive lasting business impact.

Director, Site Reliability Engineering

8x8 connects our customers and teams globally. Our XCaaS platform, the 8x8 Experience Communications Platform, brings voice, video, chat, contact center and communications APIs together in one cloud platform, so organizations can deliver better employee and customer experiences. Millions of people rely on it every day, and reliability is at the center of what we deliver.

Our engineering teams own their services in production. We are now building a central Site Reliability Engineering team with a platform-wide view. It will define how we measure reliability, build the tools and standards that help every team run their services well, and engineer shared points of failure out of the platform before they affect customers. We are looking for the Director who will build and lead it.

What will you do?

You will build 8x8's central SRE function from the ground up and lead a team across US and EU time zones. Your team will set service level objectives for our most important customer flows, improve observability and work with engineering teams to ensure the platform has the capacity and redundancy it needs. You will own the platform's dependency map and shared-infrastructure inventory, set the operational standards every service is held to, and prove through regular testing that failover works. Engineering teams keep ownership of their services. Your team covers the parts of the platform that no single team owns and raises the reliability bar for everyone.

Responsibilities

  • Build and lead a global SRE team across US and EU time zones, including its charter, operating model, hiring and career development.
  • Define the reliability strategy and multi-year roadmap for the 8x8 platform, aligned with business and customer priorities.
  • Establish SLIs, SLOs and error budgets for critical customer journeys, and use them to guide engineering priorities and balance release velocity with stability.
  • Set platform-wide standards for observability, including monitoring, logging, tracing and alerting, with a focus on actionable, customer-impacting signals.
  • Drive the reduction of operational toil through automation, self-service tooling, and infrastructure and configuration as code.
  • Partner with platform and CI/CD teams to build reliability into the software delivery lifecycle, including progressive rollouts and automated rollback.
  • Own capacity planning and performance engineering for shared infrastructure and high-traffic services.
  • Maintain a comprehensive view of service dependencies and shared infrastructure, and lead the identification and remediation of single points of failure.
  • Lead resilience and disaster recovery programs, including regular failover testing across data centers and game days for critical components.
  • Establish production readiness standards and reviews for new services and high-risk infrastructure changes.
  • Partner with the incident management team to strengthen incident response processes, and participate in high-severity incidents to provide platform-wide technical expertise and help restore service quickly.
  • Champion a blameless postmortem culture and ensure that lessons learned and corrective actions are carried through to completion.
  • Serve as a trusted reliability partner to engineering, product and executive leadership, and report on platform reliability and progress against goals.

Qualifications

Required

  • 10+ years in site reliability, infrastructure, platform or production engineering, including 5+ years leading SRE or infrastructure teams.
  • Has built or scaled an SRE or reliability function, with measurable results such as improved availability, SLO adoption or reduced toil.
  • Strong SRE practice: SLIs and SLOs, error budgets, observability, toil reduction, capacity planning, production readiness reviews and blameless postmortems.
  • Experience with incident management practices and with participating in high-severity incident response in large-scale production environments.
  • Deep infrastructure knowledge: networking, load balancers and high-availability pairs, DNS, firewalls and NAT, virtualization, and public cloud (AWS preferred).
  • Experience running services across both company-operated data centers and public cloud, including multi-site failover and disaster recovery.
  • A software engineering background: can write automation and tooling, read code and debug distributed applications.
  • Comfortable with Linux, Kubernetes, infrastructure as code (for example Terraform or Ansible), Kafka or similar messaging systems, and relational databases at scale.
  • Hands-on experience with observability tools (for example Prometheus, Grafana).
  • Can set standards and get commitments from engineering teams that do not report to you.
  • Clear communication, and the ability to explain reliability to executives in business terms.

Preferred

  • Experience with real-time communications: VoIP, SIP, WebRTC
  • Experience with enterprise load balancers and network devices such as F5, Citrix ADC or Fortinet.
  • Chaos engineering or game-day programs.
  • Service catalogs and dependency mapping (for example Backstage).
  • Experience leading teams across multiple countries and time zones.
  • Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering or a related field, or equivalent experience.

The compensation range reflects the Company’s good faith belief at the time of posting. 8x8 has different base pay ranges for different work locations within the United States, which allows us to pay employees competitively and consistently in different geographic markets. The range above reflects the potential base pay across the U.S. for this role; the applicable base pay range will depend on what ultimately is determined to be the candidate’s primary work location. jobs.title: Project Manager, Vendor Management (Early Phase) / Gestionnaire de projet, gesti
jobs.description:
Description

The Project Manager, Vendor Management ensures the successful initiation, planning, execution, monitoring, controlling and closure of assigned clinical research projects. In addition to overall project coordination, the Project Manager plays a key role in the oversight and management of study-specific vendors throughout the project lifecycle, including start-up, conduct, and closeout. This includes coordinating vendor scope, timelines, deliverables, budgets, performance, documentation, risks, issues, and escalations in close collaboration with Sponsors, vendors, and internal project teams.

The Project Manager must ensure that assigned projects and vendor-related activities are completed in compliance with the study budget, project scope and timelines and in accordance with applicable standard operating procedures (SOPs), good clinical practices, regulatory and study-specific requirements.

More specifically, the Project Manager:

  • May serve as primary contact for the Sponsor, vendors and internal team throughout the study.
  • Coordinates tasks and deadlines between the different departments involved in the project.
  • Oversees project coordinators, SSU team members, RDA and RAC resources to ensure correct prioritization of site activation activities amongst team members
  • Interacts with vendor management to ensure vendor supplies and services are coordinated for with site activation timelines
  • Escalates to project manager II when site activation timelines are at risk or cannot be maintained.
  • Assists with managing the needs and expectations of the Sponsor and other internal and external project stakeholders.
  • Assists with ensuring all team members are adequately trained on the project.
  • May plan the activities and resources (e.g. internal and external resources, equipment, etc.) required for the project.
  • Manages the quality of assigned work and deliverables
  • Assists with providing project status updates to external and internal stakeholders
  • Ensures assigned tasks are completed in compliance with the study budget, project scope and timelines and in accordance with applicable standard operating procedures (SOPs), good clinical practices, regulatory and study-specific requirements.
  • Reconciles study trackers
  • Assists with analyzing discrepancies between planned and actual results and participates in the development and implementation of corrective actions to be taken as needed.
  • Assists with enforcing effective change control and risk management throughout the project.
  • Reviews and may assist in the drafting of project operational plans, processes, and manuals as applicable (e.g., project management plan, monitoring plan, etc.).
  • Assists with ensuring that study specific documents and project deliverables (e.g., protocol, informed consent form, electronic case report form (eCRF), tables/listings/figures (TLFs), clinical study report, etc.) meet applicable country requirements.
  • Oversee activities related to sites selection (feasibility questionnaires, sites selection, planning of site qualification visits)
  • Monitors patient recruitment, subject status, and follows up with sites on recruitment strategy plan.
  • Participates in the planning and conduct of Investigator’s Meeting.
  • In collaboration with the Regulatory Affairs group, may oversee activities related to central ethics and regulatory submissions.
  • Ensures collection of required essential documents from the sites prior to study initiation and maintains of currency of site level documentation throughout the study.
  • May assist the project manager II with quality reviews and or audits of the Trial Master File (TMF) to ensure inspection readiness.
  • May support clinical monitoring activities, such as CRA training, visit report review, site letters, and escalated site issues
  • May track site qualification, initiation, routine and close-out visits, project-specific training, monitoring visit reports and follow-up letters, compliance with monitoring plan, escalation of site-related issues.
  • Maintains the project specific training matrix and confirms project team members are fully training per the study matrix prior to team members performing study tasks
  • Supports the sites and ensures that each site has the necessary material to adequately perform the study (e.g., investigational product, study supplies, special equipment, safety lab kits, etc.).
  • In collaboration with the Data Management group, may ensure that the CRF complies with the protocol and Sponsor requirements and ensures queries resolution and data review process follow the study timelines until database lock.
  • May provide technical, therapeutic and project management expertise in training and process improvement efforts for the department

Vendor Management

  • The Project Manager I will also be responsible for vendor management activities on assigned studies, including:
  • Oversees study vendors throughout the project lifecycle, ensuring delivery of services in accordance with project timelines, scope, quality expectations, and budget.
  • Acts as the primary point of contact for assigned vendors and facilitates effective communication between vendors, Sponsors, and internal project teams.
  • Reviews vendor work orders, budgets, and scope of work to ensure study requirements are accurately reflected and supports the preparation and management of change orders as required.
  • Monitors vendor performance, deliverables, timelines, and key milestones, escalating risks or performance concerns as appropriate.
  • Leads or participates in vendor meetings and documents follow-up actions to ensure timely resolution of issues.
  • Collaborates with internal subject matter experts to communicate study requirements and ensure vendor deliverables meet project expectations.
  • Reviews and approves vendor invoices, ensuring services billed are accurate and consistent with approved work orders and project progress.
  • Identifies, assesses, and manages vendor-related risks, issues, and deviations, implementing corrective actions in collaboration with vendors and internal stakeholders.
  • Supports the management of vendor quality events, including non-conformances, CAPAs, and performance improvement initiatives, in collaboration with Quality Assurance as needed.
  • Ensures vendor documentation is complete, current, and filed appropriately within the Trial Master File (TMF) and other applicable systems.
  • Tracks vendor metrics and key performance indicators (KPIs), providing updates to Sponsors and internal stakeholders as required.
  • Contributes to maintaining positive vendor relationships while ensuring vendors meet contractual obligations and project performance expectations.

Requirements

Education

  • B.Sc. in a related field of study to clinical research

Experience

  • At least 3 years of experience in a similar role, including activities related to management of clinical studies in the pharmaceutical, biotechnology and/or CRO industry
  • At least 2 years experience coordinating activities related clinical trial management

Knowledge and skills

  • Excellent knowledge of GCP and ICH standards, FDA and Canadian regulations
  • Excellent knowledge of Microsoft Office suite
  • Excellent oral and written skills in English, French is an asset
  • Excellent communication skills
  • Ability to work in a team environment and establish good relationships with colleagues and sponsors
  • Good problem-solving abilities
  • Good organizational skills
  • Strong ability to carry out different projects and work under pressure while meeting timelines
  • Experience managing small to medium projects using a disciplined approach to project management
  • Core Project Management competencies
  • Demonstrated ability to establish and deliver resource-based project plans
  • Excellent people management skills; experience working with and managing teams in a matrix environment

Our company

The Work Environment

At Indero, you will work with brilliant and driven colleagues. Our values are collaboration, innovation, reliability, and responsiveness. We offer a stimulating work environment and attractive opportunities for advancement.

In this position, you will be eligible for the following perks:

  • Flexible work schedule
  • Permanent full-time position
  • Comprehensive benefits (medical, dental, vision, RRSP, vacation, personal days, virtual medical clinic, public transportation rebates, social activities)
  • Ongoing learning and development opportunities

﻿Work Location

The successful candidate for this position has the option to work remotely anywhere in Canada, or from our headquarters in Montreal (in accordance with company policies and public health directives).

Occasional visits to our Montreal office may be required or encouraged.

About Indero

Indero is a CRO specialized in clinical trials. Based in Montreal, we have built a strong reputation for the quality of our research and services that exceed client expectations. Indero continues to grow and expand across North America and Europe.

Indero is committed to providing equitable treatment and equal opportunity to all individuals. Accommodations are available throughout the recruitment and selection process for applicants with disabilities, upon request.

Please note that Indero only accepts applicants who are legally authorized to work in Canada.

Description de poste

Le Gestionnaire de projet, Gestion des fournisseurs assure le démarrage, la planification, l’exécution, le suivi, le contrôle et la clôture réussis des projets de recherche clinique qui lui sont attribués. En plus de la coordination globale des projets, le Gestionnaire de projet joue un rôle clé dans la supervision et la gestion des fournisseurs propres à chaque étude tout au long du cycle de vie du projet, y compris lors du démarrage, de la conduite et de la clôture de l’étude. Cela comprend la coordination de la portée des activités des fournisseurs, des échéanciers, des livrables, des budgets, de la performance, de la documentation, des risques, des problèmes et des escalades, en étroite collaboration avec les Promoteurs, les fournisseurs et les équipes de projet internes.

Le Gestionnaire de projet doit s’assurer que les projets qui lui sont attribués et les activités liées aux fournisseurs sont réalisés conformément au budget de l’étude, à la portée et aux échéanciers du projet, ainsi qu’aux procédures opératoires normalisées (SOP) applicables, aux bonnes pratiques cliniques, aux exigences réglementaires et aux exigences propres à l’étude.

Plus précisément, le Chef de projet :

  • Peut agir à titre de principal point de contact pour le Promoteur, les fournisseurs et l’équipe interne pendant toute la durée de l’étude.
  • Coordonne les tâches et les échéances entre les différents services participant au projet.
  • Supervise les coordonnateurs de projet, les membres de l’équipe SSU ainsi que les ressources RDA et RAC afin d’assurer une bonne priorisation des activités d’activation des sites parmi les membres de l’équipe.
  • Collabore avec l’équipe de gestion des fournisseurs afin de s’assurer que les fournitures et les services des fournisseurs sont coordonnés en fonction des échéanciers d’activation des sites.
  • Fait remonter les problèmes au Chef de projet II lorsque les échéanciers d’activation des sites sont à risque ou ne peuvent pas être respectés.
  • Aide à gérer les besoins et les attentes du Promoteur ainsi que des autres parties prenantes internes et externes du projet.
  • Aide à s’assurer que tous les membres de l’équipe sont adéquatement formés sur le projet.
  • Peut planifier les activités et les ressources nécessaires au projet (p. ex., ressources internes et externes, équipement, etc.).
  • Gère la qualité du travail et des livrables qui lui sont attribués.
  • Aide à fournir des mises à jour sur l’état du projet aux parties prenantes externes et internes.
  • S’assure que les tâches qui lui sont attribuées sont réalisées conformément au budget de l’étude, à la portée et aux échéanciers du projet, ainsi qu’aux procédures opératoires normalisées (SOP) applicables, aux bonnes pratiques cliniques, aux exigences réglementaires et aux exigences propres à l’étude.
  • Effectue le rapprochement des outils de suivi de l’étude.
  • Aide à analyser les écarts entre les résultats prévus et les résultats réels et participe à l’élaboration et à la mise en œuvre des mesures correctives nécessaires.
  • Aide à assurer une gestion efficace des changements et des risques tout au long du projet.
  • Examine et peut contribuer à la rédaction des plans opérationnels, des processus et des manuels du projet, selon les besoins (p. ex., plan de gestion de projet, plan de monitoring, etc.).
  • Aide à s’assurer que les documents propres à l’étude et les livrables du projet (p. ex., protocole, formulaire de consentement éclairé, cahier d’observation électronique [eCRF], tableaux/listes/figures [TLF], rapport d’étude clinique, etc.) répondent aux exigences applicables dans chaque pays.
  • Supervise les activités liées à la sélection des sites (questionnaires de faisabilité, sélection des sites, planification des visites de qualification des sites).
  • Surveille le recrutement des patients et le statut des sujets, et assure le suivi auprès des sites concernant le plan stratégique de recrutement.
  • Participe à la planification et à la tenue des réunions des investigateurs.
  • En collaboration avec le groupe des Affaires réglementaires, peut superviser les activités liées aux soumissions réglementaires et aux comités d’éthique centraux.
  • S’assure que les documents essentiels requis sont recueillis auprès des sites avant le démarrage de l’étude et que la documentation au niveau des sites demeure à jour tout au long de l’étude.
  • Peut aider le Chef de projet II à effectuer des revues qualité et/ou des audits du Trial Master File (TMF) afin d’assurer l’état de préparation aux inspections.
  • Peut soutenir les activités de monitoring clinique, notamment la formation des CRA, la révision des rapports de visite, les lettres aux sites et la gestion des problèmes liés aux sites ayant fait l’objet d’une escalade.
  • Peut assurer le suivi des visites de qualification, d’initiation, de suivi régulier et de clôture des sites, des formations propres au projet, des rapports de visites de monitoring et des lettres de suivi, de la conformité au plan de monitoring ainsi que de l’escalade des problèmes liés aux sites.
  • Tient à jour la matrice de formation propre au projet et confirme que les membres de l’équipe de projet ont suivi toutes les formations requises conformément à la matrice de l’étude avant d’effectuer des tâches liées à l’étude.
  • Soutient les sites et s’assure que chacun dispose du matériel nécessaire à la bonne réalisation de l’étude (p. ex., produit expérimental, fournitures de l’étude, équipement spécialisé, trousses de laboratoire de sécurité, etc.).
  • En collaboration avec le groupe de Gestion des données, peut s’assurer que le CRF est conforme au protocole et aux exigences du Promoteur, et que la résolution des demandes de clarification et le processus de revue des données respectent les échéanciers de l’étude jusqu’au verrouillage de la base de données.
  • Peut apporter son expertise technique, thérapeutique et en gestion de projet dans le cadre des activités de formation et d’amélioration des processus du service.

﻿Gestion des fournisseurs

Gestionnaire de projet sera également responsable des activités de gestion des fournisseurs pour les études qui lui sont attribuées, notamment :

  • Supervise les fournisseurs de l’étude tout au long du cycle de vie du projet et veille à ce que les services soient fournis conformément aux échéanciers du projet, à la portée des travaux, aux attentes en matière de qualité et au budget.
  • Agit comme principal point de contact pour les fournisseurs qui lui sont attribués et facilite une communication efficace entre les fournisseurs, les Promoteurs et les équipes de projet internes.
  • Examine les bons de commande des fournisseurs, les budgets et les énoncés des travaux afin de s’assurer que les exigences de l’étude y sont correctement reflétées, et contribue à la préparation et à la gestion des demandes de modification, au besoin.
  • Surveille la performance des fournisseurs, leurs livrables, leurs échéanciers et les principales étapes du projet, et fait remonter les risques ou les préoccupations liés à la performance, selon les besoins.
  • Dirige ou participe aux réunions avec les fournisseurs et documente les mesures de suivi afin d’assurer la résolution des problèmes dans les délais prévus.
  • Collabore avec les experts internes afin de communiquer les exigences de l’étude et de s’assurer que les livrables des fournisseurs répondent aux attentes du projet.
  • Examine et approuve les factures des fournisseurs, en s’assurant que les services facturés sont exacts et conformes aux bons de commande approuvés et à l’avancement du projet.
  • Identifie, évalue et gère les risques, les problèmes et les écarts liés aux fournisseurs, et met en œuvre des mesures correctives en collaboration avec les fournisseurs et les parties prenantes internes.
  • Soutient la gestion des événements qualité liés aux fournisseurs, notamment les non-conformités, les CAPA et les initiatives d’amélioration de la performance, en collaboration avec l’Assurance qualité, au besoin.
  • S’assure que la documentation des fournisseurs est complète, à jour et classée de manière appropriée dans le Trial Master File (TMF) et les autres systèmes applicables.
  • Assure le suivi des mesures de performance des fournisseurs et des indicateurs clés de performance (KPI) et fournit des mises à jour aux Promoteurs et aux parties prenantes internes, selon les besoins.
  • Contribue au maintien de relations positives avec les fournisseurs tout en veillant à ce qu’ils respectent leurs obligations contractuelles et les attentes en matière de performance du projet.

Profil recherché

Formation

  • Baccalauréat en sciences (B. Sc.) dans un domaine lié à la recherche clinique.

Expérience

  • Au moins 3 ans d’expérience dans un rôle similaire, incluant des activités liées à la gestion d’études cliniques dans l’industrie pharmaceutique, biotechnologique et/ou au sein d’une organisation de recherche sous contrat (CRO).
  • Au moins 2 ans d’expérience dans la coordination d’activités liées à la gestion d’essais cliniques.

Connaissances et compétences

  • Excellente connaissance des bonnes pratiques cliniques (BPC/GCP), des normes de l’ICH ainsi que des réglementations de la FDA et de la réglementation canadienne.
  • Excellente maîtrise de la suite Microsoft Office.
  • Excellentes compétences en communication orale et écrite en anglais; le français constitue un atout.
  • Excellentes aptitudes en communication.
  • Capacité à travailler en équipe et à établir de bonnes relations avec les collègues et les promoteurs.
  • Bonnes capacités de résolution de problèmes.
  • Bon sens de l’organisation.
  • Grande capacité à gérer plusieurs projets et à travailler sous pression tout en respectant les échéanciers.
  • Expérience dans la gestion de projets de petite à moyenne envergure selon une approche structurée et rigoureuse de gestion de projet.
  • Maîtrise des compétences fondamentales en gestion de projet.
  • Capacité démontrée à élaborer et à exécuter des plans de projet fondés sur les ressources disponibles.
  • Excellentes compétences en gestion des personnes; expérience de travail avec des équipes et de gestion d’équipes dans un environnement matriciel.

Notre entreprise

L’environnement de travail

Chez Indero, vous travaillerez avec des collègues compétents et dynamiques. Nos valeurs sont la collaboration, l’innovation, la fiabilité et la réactivité. Nous offrons un environnement de travail stimulant ainsi que de belles perspectives d’évolution professionnelle.

Dans ce poste, vous bénéficierez des conditions suivantes :

  • Horaire de travail flexible
  • Poste permanent à temps plein
  • Gamme complète d’avantages sociaux (assurances médicales, dentaires, vision, régime de retraite, vacances, journées personnelles, clinique médicale virtuelle, rabais sur le transport en commun, activités sociales)
  • Formation et développement continu

Lieu de travail

La personne embauchée pourra travailler à distance de n’importe quelle ville au Canada, ou depuis notre bureau principal à Montréal (conformément aux politiques de l’entreprise et aux directives de santé publique).

Des visites occasionnelles à notre siège social pourraient être requises ou encouragées.

﻿À propos d’Indero

Indero est une entreprise de recherche clinique contractuelle (CRO) spécialisée dans les essais cliniques. Depuis ses débuts, notre entreprise à taille humaine s’est forgé une solide réputation pour la qualité de ses recherches et de ses services, surpassant les attentes de nos clients. Basée à Montréal, Indero poursuit sa croissance à travers l’Amérique du Nord et l’Europe.

Indero s’engage à offrir un traitement équitable et des chances égales à tous les candidats. Des accommodements peuvent être offerts à toute étape du processus de recrutement pour les personnes en situation de handicap, sur demande.

Indero n’accepte que les candidatures de personnes légalement autorisées à travailler au Canada.

Le genre masculin est utilisé sans discrimination, dans le seul but d’alléger le texte.

jobs.title: Clinical Assistant
jobs.description:
Description

Are you looking to make a difference in patients’ lives with a company that values your expertise? Join us in our mission of delivering compassionate healthcare where it matters most –– at home.

Pinnacle Home Care, Florida’s largest Medicare-certified home health provider, has been delivering high-quality, patient-centered care for over two decades, and we’re looking for a Clinical Assistant/ Scheduler to join our award-winning team.

Key Responsibilities

  • Schedules patients for the entirety of visit plans at the beginning of each episode, ensuring consistency and continuity of care.
  • Ensures clinician efficiency by utilizing the productivity spreadsheet. Updates the spreadsheet to identify opportunities and maintain appropriate staffing levels. Reports deficiencies and failures to meet full-time standards and PRN clinician requirements to the Clinical Manager.
  • Complies with Pending SOC standard operating procedures to process incoming referrals accurately and on time. Strives to achieve admission within 24 hours of referral receipt for each patient.
  • Reviews and reports daily to Care Coordinators and Clinical Managers all Pending SOCs that were scheduled but not admitted.
  • Documents updates on patient care and scheduling adjustments in communication notes.
  • Schedules new hire clinicians in accordance with ramp-up expectations.
  • Schedules resumptions of care following facility discharge and in alignment with Clinical Review Team notes.
  • Works one major and one minor holiday per calendar year and provides availability for one weekend per month.
  • Maintains patient and employee confidentiality in accordance with HIPAA regulations and agency standards.
  • Performs other duties and activities as delegated by the Branch Clinical Manager or Scheduling Manager.
  • Schedules, reschedules, and manages patient visits across all disciplines in accordance with the plan of care, frequency orders, and episode timelines.
  • Monitors underscheduled visits to prevent missed or delayed care.
  • Ensures adequate staffing coverage for callouts, PTO, weekends, and holidays.
  • Balances clinician productivity, geographic considerations, and availability when scheduling.
  • Navigates and manages workflows within the WellSky EMR, including Resource Manager, Episode Manager, and task queues.

Requirements

Qualifications

  • Must be a High School graduate.
  • Demonstrates strong attention to detail, ensuring accuracy in scheduling, reporting, and documentation while maintaining compliance with policies and procedures.
  • Exhibits strong organizational skills to balance multiple tasks, manage time efficiently, and ensure the seamless execution of scheduling processes.
  • Communicates effectively through clear verbal and written communication, facilitating collaboration and keeping all team members informed.
  • Works well in a collaborative team environment, fostering positive relationships with colleagues and clinicians to support efficient achievement of patient care goals.
  • Applies strong problem-solving skills to identify scheduling challenges and operational issues, implementing practical solutions to maintain smooth workflows and optimized resource utilization.
  • Demonstrates adaptability by adjusting to changing schedules, priorities, and unforeseen circumstances in a fast-paced healthcare environment.

Benefits

Why Choose Pinnacle?

  • Personalized, One-on-One Care: Help patients heal and regain their independence by delivering individualized care in the comfort of their homes.
  • Growth & Stability: Over two decades as Florida’s largest independent home health agency.
  • Ongoing Professional Development: Free Continuing Education Units (CEUs) to support licensure and career advancement.
  • Competitive Benefits & Perks: Including an employee referral program where you can earn rewards.
  • Recognized Excellence: Ranked as a USA Today Top Workplace.
  • Flexible Scheduling: Enjoy a schedule that aligns with your personal priorities.
  • Supportive & Fun Culture: Join a collaborative, forward-thinking team that values both professional excellence and personal fulfillment.

Pinnacle promotes an inclusive environment and is an equal opportunity employer. We prohibit discrimination or harassment based on race, religion, age, gender, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected characteristics.

Be part of a company that empowers clinicians to make a difference in the lives of over 10,000 patients across Florida every day. Apply now!
