jobs.title: Principal Software Engineer - Document Processing (US Remote)
jobs.description:
TREND Health Partners is a tech-enabled payment integrity company. Our mission is to facilitate collaboration between payers and providers for mutual benefit and waste reduction, ultimately improving access to healthcare. We achieve this by aligning the common goals of payers and providers and fostering collaboration through a shared technology platform and seamless workflows.
Joining TREND Health Partners means becoming part of a dynamic, growing organization that promotes a collaborative and innovative work environment. Our comprehensive compensation package includes competitive salaries, highly valued health insurance, a 401(k) plan with employer match, paid parental leave, and more.
The Principal Software Engineer will lead the development of innovative, scalable software solutions that support complex document review workflows for healthcare payers and providers. This role requires a deep understanding of modern web application architecture and cloud-native backend systems. The engineer will collaborate closely with architects, product, QA, and cloud teams to drive system-wide design decisions, optimize platform performance, and deliver new capabilities to our customers.
The ideal candidate will possess strong technical leadership, a hands-on approach to coding, and the ability to mentor other engineers while ensuring alignment with architectural standards and business goals.

Role and Responsibilities

  • Lead the evolution of our document processing pipeline: designing Step Functions state machines, writing the modular Go services that run inside them, and defining contracts that let workflow steps be swapped in and out cleanly.
  • Own the hard problems around processing real-world PDFs reliably at scale — malformed input, structural variance, and performance across documents from a few pages to tens of thousands.
  • Build out operational metrics and observability — starting with the document pipeline, extending to other platform areas as needs surface.
  • Take a concept from "here's roughly the problem" to a shipped, working solution with minimal hand-holding.
  • Mentor and grow the other engineers working in this space, and advocate for the pipeline's forward progress.
  • Contribute to database design and query performance across our Postgres/RDS environment.
  • Work with OpenSearch for indexing and search functionality tied to document data.
  • Support the wider platform ecosystem beyond the core pipeline as needs come up.
  • Review code, weigh in on architecture, and help set technical direction for the team.
  • Partner with product and engineering leads to turn loose requirements into real technical designs.

Qualifications

  • Documented professional software engineering experience, with a track record of shipping and operating production systems — we're looking at what you've built and owned, not just tenure.
  • A habit of taking ownership of the problem space, driving the solution, and standing behind your decisions. We don't do blame here — when something goes wrong, we own it, learn, and move forward.
  • Strong Go experience, particularly for backend/service work.
  • Hands-on experience with document processing at scale — you understand PDF structure and edge cases well enough to reason about performance, reliability, and failure modes across variable real-world input.
  • Experience designing and implementing metrics and observability for production systems — deciding what should be measured and building it, not just consuming dashboards someone else built.
  • Comfort with AWS serverless patterns: Lambda, Step Functions, ECS, and event-driven architecture generally.
  • Solid database fundamentals — schema design, query optimization, troubleshooting performance issues.
  • A track record of driving something from an ambiguous starting point to a finished product.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound calls without a lot of oversight.
  • Strong communication — you'll need to explain tradeoffs to engineers and non-engineers alike.
  • Experience mentoring engineers day to day — not just leaving comments in code review, but actively growing the people around you.
  • Comfort handling sensitive data (PHI) responsibly and in line with HIPAA requirements.

​Preferred Skills​

  • Proficiency in C++ — not required, but a plus given some of our high-performance pipeline segments are written in it.
  • Interest or experience in Rust — not currently in use, but on the table for future performance-critical pipeline work.
  • Hands-on OpenSearch (or Lucene-based search) experience. This space doesn't have a dedicated owner today — if it's a strength of yours, there's a real opportunity to take charge of it.
  • Experience with document-centric pipelines (OCR, classification, extraction, or similar).
  • Healthcare or payment-integrity industry background.
  • Comfort using agentic coding tools as part of a modern dev workflow.

    A Note on Culture

    We're a laid-back team — plenty of memes, self-managed accountability, low ceremony. We care more about whether the work is good and the pipeline is reliable than about how you got there. We're Mac-shop, and we lean on modern tooling (including AI-assisted coding) without letting it replace engineering judgment.

Mental and Physical Demands

  • This position will be exposed mainly to an indoor office environment and will be expected to work in or around computers and printers.
  • The nature of the work is sedentary, and the employee will be sitting most of the time.
  • Essential physical functions of the job include typing and the repetitive motion to utilize computer software and hardware continuously throughout the day.
  • Essential mental functions of this position include concentrating on analytical tasks, reading information, and verbal/written communication to others continuously throughout the day.

Related Duties As Assigned

  • This job description documents the general nature and level of work but is not intended to be a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities required for this position. Consequently, employee’s may be asked to perform other duties as required.
  • Employees may also be asked to complete certain compliance requirements set forth by our Business Partners in the performance of their jobs including but not limited to requests for background and drug screenings and disclosures of personal health information or personally identifiable information. Exemptions as provided under the ADA and TITLE VII of the Civil Rights Act will be observed and followed.
  • Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the functions outlined above.

jobs.title: Lead Legal Counsel, Capital Markets
jobs.description:
About Upstart

At Upstart, we’re united by a mission that matters: to radically reduce the cost and complexity of borrowing for all Americans. Every day, we bring creativity, experimentation, and advanced AI to reshape access to credit, helping millions move forward financially with clarity and confidence.

As the leading AI lending marketplace, we partner with banks and credit unions to expand access to affordable credit through technology that’s both radically intelligent and deeply human. Our platform runs over one million predictions per borrower using more than 3,000 signals, powering smarter, fairer decisions for millions of customers. But the numbers only hint at the impact. Every idea, every voice, and every contribution moves us closer to a world where credit never stands between people and their financial progress.

We’re proudly digital-first, giving most Upstarters the flexibility to do their best work from wherever they thrive, alongside teammates across 80+ cities in the US and Canada. Digital-first doesn’t mean distant. We’re intentional about in-person connection through team onsites, planning sessions, and moments that spark creativity and trust. And whether you choose to work primarily from home or collaborate in-person from one of our offices in Columbus, Austin, the Bay Area, or New York City, you’ll have the support to work in the way that works best for you.

If you’re energized by tackling meaningful problems, excited to innovate with purpose, and motivated by work that truly matters, we’d love to hear from you.

The Team:

Upstart’s capital markets legal team is at the forefront of creating innovative deal structures that drive our business forward. We negotiate deals that push the envelope on deal terms in a thoughtful, strategic manner. By partnering with the capital markets business team, we exert a tremendous impact on the overall amount of funding that Upstart is able to obtain each year.

As the Lead Legal Counsel, Capital Markets at Upstart, you will work with counterparties across Upstart including members of the product, operations, compliance, accounting, tax, treasury and finance teams. You will work on bilateral deals, small club deals, broadly syndicated deals and everything in between.

How you’ll make an impact

  • Support the capital markets and finance teams in purchase and sale agreements, securitization transactions, other liquidity arrangements and day-to-day operational and legal support
  • Review, draft and negotiate a variety of transactional documents opposite sophisticated institutional investors, including asset managers, private equity funds, hedge funds and pension funds
  • Manage deal flow and work with outside counsel in structuring and executing various securitization transactions, including pass-throughs and asset-backed securitizations
  • Collaborate with a variety of internal and external stakeholders (including other members of the legal team) as new products are launched, ensuring consistency across documents and providing subject matter expertise over capital markets and investor channels
  • Develop processes and maintain/ improve templates for transactions to support and drive rapidly growing business.
  • Partner with product-regulatory colleagues to anticipate and address regulatory cross-winds
  • Create internal education on a variety of legal risks

Minimum Qualifications

  • J.D. degree with solid academic credentials and a state bar membership
  • 10+ years of work experience, including both large law firm and in-house experience (in structured finance, debt finance or similar)
  • Experienced in drafting and negotiating sophisticated transactional documents
  • Strong communication skills with a demonstrated ability to effectively and proactively provide quick, concise, and practical legal advice
  • Experience managing a team

Preferred Qualifications

  • Prior experience at a fintech company focused on lending /credit markets
  • CA or NY bar membership
  • Proven ability to develop scalable processes and procedures
  • Eager to develop expertise in new or unfamiliar products and areas of law

Position location This role is available in the following locations: Remote

Time zone requirements The team operates on the East/West coast time zones.

Travel requirements As a digital first company, the majority of your work can be accomplished remotely. The majority of our employees can live and work anywhere in the U.S but are encouraged to to still spend high quality time in-person collaborating via regular onsites. The in-person sessions’ cadence varies depending on the team and role; most teams meet once or twice per quarter for 2-4 consecutive days at a time.

At Upstart, your base pay is one part of your total compensation package. The anticipated base salary for this position is expected to be within the below range. Your actual base pay will depend on your geographic location–with our “digital first” philosophy, Upstart uses compensation regions that vary depending on location. Individual pay is also determined by job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training. Your recruiter can share more about the specific salary range for your preferred location during the hiring process.

In addition, Upstart provides employees with target bonuses, equity compensation, and generous benefits packages (including medical, dental, vision, and 401k).

United States | Remote - Anticipated Base Salary Range
$208,000—$287,900 USD

What you'll love

At Upstart, our benefits for full-time employees are designed to support your health, financial well-being, family, and personal growth. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Competitive compensation, including base pay, bonus opportunities, and annual equity grants that vest quarterly
  • Retirement benefits to help you plan for the future, including a 401(k) or Group Retirement Savings Plan with a company match of $2 for every $1 contributed, up to $15,000 annually (USD in the US, CAD in Canada)
  • Employee Stock Purchase Plan (ESPP) with discounted stock purchase options for eligible employees (US only)
  • Comprehensive health coverage designed to support you and your family, including medical, dental, vision, and wellness resources for US and supplemental health coverage for Canada.
  • Health Savings Account contributions from Upstart for eligible plans (US only)
  • Income protection benefits, including life insurance and disability coverage for added financial security
  • Paid time off, sick leave, and company holidays, in line with local requirements
  • Paid family and parental leave to support caregiving and major life moments (duration varies by country)
  • Family-centered benefits to support fertility, parenthood, and caregiving needs
  • Employee Assistance Program (EAP) offering mental health support and life-centered resources
  • Financial wellness resources, including access to financial planning tools and a financial concierge service (US Only)
  • Annual wellness allowance to support your physical and emotional well-being and personal development, based on what matters most to you
  • Annual productivity allowance to invest in relevant tools and resources you need to do your best work, no matter where you work from
  • Connection and community through team events, all-company updates, and employee resource groups (ERGs)
  • Onsite perks, including catered lunches and fully stocked micro-kitchens when working from one of our offices in the Bay Area, Austin, Columbus, and New York City

For roles based in Canada, please note that we are not currently able to hire in Quebec.

Upstart is a proud Equal Opportunity Employer. Just as we are dedicated to improving access to affordable credit for all, we are committed to inclusive and fair hiring practices.

jobs.description:
Job Description: English Language Expert – United States

Role Type: Contractor
Location: Remote, United States

About the Role

We are seeking English Language Experts based in the United States to support a specialized audio annotation project focused on American English. In this role, you will use your language expertise to help improve AI systems through accurate audio analysis, transcription review, and linguistic annotation.

Candidates with backgrounds in language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or other language-focused fields are encouraged to apply. Familiarity with the diverse range of American English dialects and accents is highly valued.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Listen to multi-speaker conversational audio and analyze linguistic content for annotation.
  2. Tag audio samples and speakers with relevant metadata, including dialect, accent, speaking style, age, audio quality, and background noise.
  3. Review and correct automatic speech recognition (ASR) transcripts, ensuring accuracy and consistency with American English spelling and usage.
  4. Identify and annotate regional and cultural language variations, including Southern English, African American Vernacular English (AAVE), New York City English, Midwestern English, and other varieties.
  5. Apply knowledge of American idioms, slang, and vocabulary to validate and improve transcript quality.

Preferred Qualifications

  1. Fluency in American English, with a strong understanding of US dialects and pronunciation variations.
  2. Experience in linguistics, language teaching, transcription, editing, translation, journalism, or a related field.
  3. Ability to recognize and describe regional American accents and cultural language variations.
  4. Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong attention to detail.

As a senior team member, you'll help establish effective troubleshooting practices and may provide technical guidance to less-experienced support engineers.

This is a senior individual-contributor role focused on technical support execution and problem resolution, not formal people management.

We're looking for someone with substantial experience supporting SaaS applications, strong debugging skills, and the ability to communicate clearly under pressure.

You should be comfortable investigating ambiguous technical issues, organizing evidence, and working across teams to drive resolution.

jobs.title: Backend Engineer, New Grad
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Backend Engineer, New Grad to join Bask Health's engineering team and help build the software infrastructure behind our telehealth platform.

This role is designed for recent graduates and early-career engineers who have strong programming fundamentals, enjoy building software, and want to gain hands-on experience developing production backend systems.

You'll work on APIs, databases, backend services, and application logic that support patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and merchant tools.

Our engineering stack includes TypeScript, Node.js, AWS, SST, and SQL databases, with technologies such as Prisma and Drizzle used across the platform.

You'll collaborate with experienced engineers, receive feedback through code reviews, and gradually take ownership of more complex features as your technical skills develop.

We're looking for someone who is curious, takes initiative, learns quickly, and enjoys understanding how software works beyond the code they're assigned to write.

You don't need years of professional experience or previous healthcare industry experience. We care about your technical foundation, the projects you've built, your ability to solve problems, and your willingness to learn.

What You'll Do

  • Build, test, and maintain backend features that support Bask's telehealth platform.
  • Develop APIs, application logic, and backend services using TypeScript and Node.js.
  • Work with SQL databases to create, update, and retrieve application data.
  • Help implement backend functionality for patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and merchant tools.
  • Learn how our serverless infrastructure works using AWS, SST, and related technologies.
  • Assist with building and maintaining integrations between internal services and third-party APIs.
  • Write clean, readable, maintainable code that follows established engineering practices.
  • Create automated tests to verify functionality and help prevent regressions.
  • Debug application issues, investigate errors, and work with experienced engineers to resolve problems.
  • Participate in code reviews and learn how to give and receive constructive technical feedback.
  • Collaborate with frontend engineers to understand how APIs connect to user-facing applications.
  • Work with product managers and engineers to understand requirements and break projects into manageable tasks.
  • Learn how to design database schemas, structure backend services, and organize application logic.
  • Help maintain documentation for APIs, backend features, and development workflows.
  • Use AI-assisted development tools such as Cursor and Claude Code to explore solutions, understand unfamiliar code, and accelerate development while validating generated code.
  • Learn how to test changes in staging environments before releasing them to production.
  • Assist with monitoring, logging, and troubleshooting backend services.
  • Contribute to improving existing code, reducing technical debt, and simplifying development workflows.
  • Take ownership of smaller features and gradually work toward independently delivering more complex projects.
  • Ask questions, share ideas, and actively participate in technical discussions.
  • Develop an understanding of security, data privacy, and reliability requirements for healthcare applications.
  • Continue building your technical skills through hands-on projects, feedback, and collaboration with the engineering team.

Requirements

  • Recently completed or currently completing a degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • Strong understanding of programming fundamentals, data structures, algorithms, and basic software design principles.
  • Familiarity with JavaScript, TypeScript, or another modern programming language, with an interest in developing backend applications using TypeScript and Node.js.
  • Experience building software through coursework, internships, personal projects, open-source contributions, or professional work.
  • Basic understanding of how APIs, servers, and web applications communicate.
  • Familiarity with relational databases and basic SQL concepts.
  • Understanding of Git or another version control system.

Company Overview

By Light Professional IT Services LLC readies warfighters and federal agencies with technology and systems engineered to connect, protect, and prepare individuals and teams for whatever comes next. Headquartered in McLean, VA, By Light supports defense, civilian, and commercial IT customers worldwide.

Position Overview

By Light is seeking an experienced Senior Solutions Architect to serve as the lead architect for RangeOS, our cyber range and training platform supporting Department of Defense cyberspace operations.

The architect is the strategic and technical bridge between business goals, user needs, and engineering execution. This individual owns the overall structure, components, and integration of RangeOS so the platform remains feasible, scalable, secure, and aligned with product and business objectives.

This is a technically grounded leadership role. The architect leads a team of engineers, works directly with product management, DevSecOps, and engineering leads, and guides architectural decisions from initial design through deployment and sustainment. Customer relationship ownership resides with program leadership; the architect supports those engagements as the senior technical authority on the platform.

Responsibilities

Product Architecture & Technical Framework

  • Define and own the RangeOS technical architecture, including system components, interactions, data flows, and core technologies.
  • Ensure the architecture meets both functional and non-functional requirements, including scalability, reliability, performance, and security.
  • Make forward-looking design decisions so the platform can grow, handle increasing load, and remain maintainable over its lifecycle.
  • Design backend services, microservices, RESTful APIs, and distributed application architectures.
  • Provide technical direction across the full stack, including frontend frameworks, backend services, databases, and system integrations.
  • Evaluate existing components and lead modernization of legacy capabilities into containerized, cloud-native architectures.
  • Technology Selection & Roadmap
  • Select and evaluate tools, frameworks, languages, and platforms based on performance, cost, scalability, security, and team expertise.
  • Build and maintain the RangeOS technical roadmap in partnership with product management, aligned with the product roadmap.
  • Maintain architecture documentation, standards, and decision records so the platform is clear and maintainable as it evolves.
  • Translate business and user requirements into technical specifications, and translate technical constraints back into product terms.

Cloud-Native Architecture & DevSecOps

  • Architect containerized applications using Kubernetes, Docker, and related orchestration technologies.
  • Design solutions for cloud, hybrid cloud, and on-premises deployment environments.
  • Partner with DevSecOps engineers on secure, automated build, test, integration, and deployment pipelines.
  • Guide the use of CI/CD, Infrastructure as Code, configuration management, and automated deployment.
  • Incorporate security, observability, fault tolerance, and performance into the architecture from the start.

Risk & Technical Debt Management

Team Leadership

RangeOS Technology Environment

jobs.title: Sales Development Representative
jobs.description:
Propeller is on a mission to take the guesswork out of moving dirt - reducing wasted fuel, time, and money. We do this through the power of maps.

Our customers use Propeller's integrated hardware and software products to capture accurate 3D versions of their worksites. With over 50,000 worksites worldwide using Propeller's smart survey technology, we empower project teams to map, measure, and manage site activity.

Propeller empowers everyone to approach, own, and solve problems creatively. We're data nerds who care about impact, honesty, and each other. We take pride in being a great place to work and are proud to be recognized as a Fast Company and BuiltIn Best Place to Work. You can learn more about us on Glassdoor.

About the role

There's a big opportunity for Propeller to reach more customers across the UK and EMEA. We're building a stronger direct route to market as we grow, and you'll play an important part in making that happen.

As a Sales Development Representative, you'll own the first stage of our sales journey. You'll identify businesses that could benefit from Propeller, start meaningful conversations, understand the challenges they're facing and turn those conversations into qualified sales opportunities.

You'll help us open new markets, build relationships with potential customers and create momentum for new customer growth. You'll work closely with the UK sales team and our SDR colleagues in the US, partnering with Account Executives to make sure potential customers have a great experience from their very first interaction with Propeller.

You'll have room to take ownership of your market, develop your sales skills and learn what it takes to build a successful sales career.

What you’re accountable for

Building outbound pipeline. Identify businesses and people who could benefit from Propeller and find creative ways to get their attention. Reach out through calls, email and other channels, experiment with different approaches and build a consistent flow of new conversations and opportunities.

Making the most of inbound interest. Connect with people who have already shown an interest in Propeller. Understand what they're looking for, explore whether we're the right fit and help turn that initial interest into meaningful sales conversations.

Understanding your market. Build a strong understanding of the companies, industries and people we should be speaking to across the UK and other EMEA markets. Research potential customers, develop prospect lists and identify new ways to reach the right people.

Creating great customer conversations. Ask thoughtful questions and listen closely to understand how potential customers work, what challenges they're facing and where Propeller could help. Qualify opportunities and work closely with Account Executives to make sure the next steps are relevant, well-informed and valuable for the customer.

Learning and improving. Get to know our product, customers and sales approach inside out. Pay attention to what's working, share what you're learning and look for ways to improve how we reach and engage potential customers. Take feedback on board and keep developing your approach.

Requirements

  • Based in: United Kingdom
  • Fluent English is essential. Speaking another language fluently is a plus.
  • Some experience in a sales environment where you've worked towards targets or built relationships with potential customers. That could be in recruitment, software, a startup or another sales setting.
  • You're comfortable picking up the phone, making cold calls and starting conversations with people who don't know us yet.
  • You communicate clearly, both in writing and in conversation.
  • You're curious about people and their challenges, and know how to listen before jumping into a pitch.
  • You take ownership, follow through and can keep yourself moving when working independently and remotely.
  • You're interested in technology and enjoy learning how products work and explaining their value in a way that makes sense to customers.
  • You're open to feedback, willing to try new things, learn from them and keep improving.
  • Experience in SaaS or an industry we serve, such as construction, civil engineering or mining, is a plus.

Benefits

  • Remote working + 3 team meetups a year in great European cities
  • Employee share options
  • Professional development benefits and leave
  • Monthly telephone and/or internet allowance
  • WFH equipment provided

About Propeller

Propeller is for everyone, so come as you are. We value all types of experience, skill, and ability. If you don't think you meet all the requirements, but still think this role would be a good fit, we'd love to hear from you.

Diversity makes our team more creative, fun, and effective, so bring your whole self to the application process, and we will too!

If you're interested in what life at Propeller is like, check out our employee-owned Medium blog page!

jobs.description:
Resumen del puesto

El Process Analyst Low Code e IA Copilot es responsable de analizar, rediseñar y optimizar procesos de negocio mediante el uso de plataformas Low Code y capacidades de Inteligencia Artificial (Copilots), transformando operaciones manuales o ineficientes en flujos automatizados, escalables y orientados a datos.

Su misión es identificar oportunidades de mejora, automatización y generación de valor mediante la combinación de análisis de procesos, automatización inteligente, analítica y herramientas de IA generativa, trabajando de forma colaborativa con equipos de negocio, tecnología, datos y operaciones para impulsar eficiencia, productividad y toma de decisiones basada en información.

Este rol combina pensamiento analítico, automatización, mejora continua, data-driven mindset y adopción de IA aplicada al negocio.

Responsabilidades principales

Analizar procesos actuales (AS-IS) para identificar ineficiencias, cuellos de botella, riesgos y oportunidades de automatización.

Levantar, documentar y modelar procesos de negocio utilizando BPMN, diagramas de flujo y herramientas colaborativas.

Diseñar procesos optimizados (TO-BE) alineados a objetivos de eficiencia, escalabilidad y experiencia del usuario interno/externo.

Identificar oportunidades de automatización mediante herramientas Low Code / No Code y plataformas de IA Copilot.

Configurar y construir automatizaciones, flujos y aplicaciones Low Code para optimizar procesos operativos y administrativos.

Integrar capacidades de IA generativa y copilots para mejorar productividad, análisis de información y soporte a la toma de decisiones.

Definir métricas, KPIs y dashboards que permitan monitorear el desempeño de procesos y automatizaciones implementadas.

Colaborar con equipos de Business Intelligence y Data para asegurar trazabilidad, calidad y explotación de datos generados por los procesos.

Participar en iniciativas de mejora continua, transformación digital y eficiencia operativa.

Capacitar y acompañar a equipos de negocio en la adopción de automatizaciones y herramientas de IA.

Documentar procesos, automatizaciones, aprendizajes y buenas prácticas de optimización y automatización.

Participar activamente en marcos ágiles y de mejora continua (Scrum, Kanban, Lean), aportando visión analítica y de eficiencia operativa.

Promover la adopción de una cultura data-driven, automatización y uso responsable de IA en la organización.

Requisitos

Experiencia mínima de 3 años en análisis, mejora y optimización de procesos de negocio.

Experiencia trabajando con automatización de procesos, transformación digital o iniciativas de eficiencia operativa.

Conocimientos en modelado de procesos (BPMN, diagramas de flujo, SIPOC, VSM).

Experiencia con herramientas Low Code / No Code (Power Platform, AppSheet, OutSystems, Mendix, Zapier u otras).

Experiencia utilizando herramientas de IA generativa o copilots aplicados al trabajo (automatización, análisis, documentación, productividad).

Capacidad para traducir necesidades de negocio en automatizaciones y soluciones tecnológicas simples y escalables.

Conocimiento en análisis de datos y métricas de procesos (KPIs, dashboards, seguimiento de performance).

Experiencia colaborando con equipos de negocio, tecnología y datos.

Habilidad para documentar procesos, crear guías y generar estandarización operativa.

Deseable experiencia en entornos ágiles, proyectos de automatización o transformación digital.

Excelentes habilidades de comunicación, pensamiento analítico, resolución de problemas y orientación a resultados.

Mentalidad de mejora continua, curiosidad tecnológica y enfoque en eficiencia y automatización.

jobs.title: Patient Support Associate
jobs.description:
About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, we understand that reliable support is an important part of a good software experience. We value people who communicate clearly, pay attention to details, follow through on their responsibilities, and know when to involve the right team to resolve an issue.

About the Role

We're looking for a Patient Support Associate to assist with routine, non-clinical patient support requests within Bask Health's telehealth platform, subject to the approved responsibilities of our patient support operations.

This is a hands-on support role for someone who enjoys solving problems, communicating with people, and making sure requests are handled accurately.

You'll help patients navigate supported platform workflows, troubleshoot basic software issues, and understand the appropriate next steps when they encounter a problem.

You'll be responsible for documenting support requests, following established procedures, and escalating matters that require specialized assistance.

Bask Health provides software that helps entrepreneurs and healthcare businesses launch and manage direct-to-consumer telehealth services.

The platform brings together patient-facing experiences, merchant storefronts, questionnaires, checkout workflows, clinical processes, and pharmacy-related operations.

You'll develop a practical understanding of the non-clinical software workflows relevant to your assigned responsibilities.

You'll assist patients who have questions about accessing or navigating supported platform features.

You'll help users understand approved instructions for completing non-clinical steps.

You'll provide assistance with routine platform access and navigation issues.

You'll help identify problems that prevent users from progressing through expected software workflows.

You'll follow approved troubleshooting steps before escalating an issue.

You'll gather relevant details when a patient reports a software problem.

You'll document the issue clearly so another team member can understand what happened.

You'll use approved support systems to create, update, and manage assigned tickets.

You'll organize your queue and track open requests that require additional action.

You'll help ensure support tickets contain accurate descriptions, relevant context, and appropriate next steps.

You'll follow established procedures for categorizing and prioritizing requests.

You'll respond to patients through approved communication channels, which may include email, chat, or other designated systems.

You'll communicate clearly and professionally, especially when someone is confused or frustrated.

You'll avoid unnecessary technical language when explaining routine software issues.

You'll make sure patients understand what actions they can take and what the support team will do next.

You'll avoid making promises about resolution times or outcomes unless those commitments are supported by approved procedures.

You'll follow through on assigned requests until they are resolved or appropriately transferred.

You'll recognize when a problem cannot be resolved using standard troubleshooting procedures.

You'll escalate technical issues to the appropriate support or engineering team.

You'll provide clear descriptions of the problem and any troubleshooting already completed.

You'll coordinate with other internal teams when additional information is required.

You'll keep support records updated as issues progress.

You'll communicate approved updates to patients when an issue remains unresolved.

You'll help prevent requests from being overlooked or left without appropriate ownership.

You'll work with customer success or merchant support teams when a problem involves a merchant-controlled platform configuration.

You'll follow established ownership boundaries between Bask Health, merchants, healthcare providers, and pharmacies.

You'll recognize when a question concerns medication, diagnosis, treatment, prescription decisions, or other clinical matters.

You'll refer those questions to the appropriate licensed or authorized healthcare professional.

You'll recognize when a question involves prescription fulfillment, dispensing, medication preparation, or pharmacy operations.

You'll direct pharmacy-specific concerns to the appropriate authorized team.

You'll never provide medical advice, interpret clinical information, recommend medications, or make treatment decisions.

You'll avoid making statements about whether a patient will be approved for treatment.

You'll avoid guaranteeing prescription availability, dispensing outcomes, or medication delivery dates.

You'll follow established privacy, security, and information-handling procedures.

You'll use approved identity verification procedures before discussing account-specific information.

You'll access only the information necessary and authorized for your responsibilities.

You'll use designated communication and support systems when handling sensitive information.

You'll recognize and report suspected privacy or security concerns.

You'll help maintain accurate support documentation and internal knowledge resources.

You'll use approved troubleshooting guides to resolve common issues consistently.

You'll identify outdated instructions or unclear support procedures and bring them to the appropriate team.

You'll help document recurring support questions and technical problems.

You'll share patterns that may indicate a broader software issue.

You'll collaborate with technical support, product, and engineering teams when appropriate.

You'll provide clear feedback about common errors, confusing platform steps, and recurring user difficulties.

You'll participate in training when platform features or support procedures change.

You'll learn how to use internal support tools and follow established workflows.

You'll manage multiple requests while maintaining attention to detail.

You'll prioritize requests according to approved guidelines rather than personal assumptions.

You'll ask for assistance when a situation falls outside your knowledge or authority.

You'll maintain a calm and professional approach during challenging interactions.

You'll take responsibility for accurate documentation and timely follow-up.

You'll help ensure support requests are routed to the correct teams.

You'll contribute to a consistent support experience by following established standards.

You'll work with colleagues to identify opportunities for improving ticket handling and internal communication.

You'll be comfortable working independently while staying connected with a remote team.

You'll communicate proactively when you encounter obstacles or need clarification.

You'll remain flexible as software workflows and support procedures evolve.

You'll help improve the reliability and consistency of routine patient support operations.

We're looking for someone with customer-facing support experience, strong written communication skills, and the ability to follow detailed procedures.

You should be comfortable using web-based software, documenting issues, and coordinating with other teams when a request requires additional assistance.

Previous healthcare or telehealth experience would be helpful, but this is not a clinical position.

Success in this role means resolving routine non-clinical support requests accurately, maintaining organized support records, escalating specialized concerns appropriately, and ensuring patients receive clear and reliable communication.

What You'll Do

  • Respond to assigned non-clinical patient support requests through approved channels.
  • Assist patients with routine platform access and navigation questions.
  • Help users follow approved instructions for supported software workflows.
  • Troubleshoot basic technical issues using established procedures.
  • Create, update, and manage assigned support tickets.
  • Document reported problems and troubleshooting steps accurately.
  • Categorize and prioritize support requests according to approved guidelines.
  • Track open issues and follow-up responsibilities.
  • Communicate clearly and professionally with patients.
  • Provide approved instructions and next steps for routine issues.
  • Escalate unresolved technical problems to the appropriate teams.
  • Coordinate with technical support and engineering when necessary.
  • Maintain accurate records as support requests progress.
  • Follow through on assigned issues until resolution or appropriate handoff.
  • Coordinate with merchant support teams when requests involve merchant-controlled workflows.
  • Recognize questions that require clinical or pharmacy expertise.
  • Refer medical and treatment-related questions to authorized healthcare professionals.
  • Refer pharmacy-specific matters to authorized pharmacy contacts.
  • Avoid providing medical advice or making clinical decisions.
  • Follow approved identity verification and access control procedures.
  • Protect sensitive information and comply with applicable privacy and security requirements.
  • Use approved systems when handling patient-related information.
  • Report suspected privacy or security concerns.
  • Identify recurring technical problems and support questions.
  • Contribute to internal troubleshooting guides and knowledge resources.
  • Share relevant issue patterns with support and product teams.
  • Participate in training on software updates and support procedures.
  • Manage multiple assigned tickets while maintaining accuracy.
  • Follow established service quality and escalation standards.
  • Ask for guidance when requests fall outside approved procedures.
  • Support improvements to ticket management and internal communication.
  • Take ownership of assigned support responsibilities and follow through consistently.

Requirements

  • At least 1 year of experience in customer support, customer service, patient services, or a similar customer-facing role.
  • Experience responding to customer questions and resolving routine support concerns.
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to explain software-related steps clearly and simply.
  • Comfortable navigating web-based software platforms.

  • Ability to remain calm and organized under pressure.
  • Willingness to follow strict boundaries around clinical and medical information.
  • Understanding of the importance of privacy and secure information handling.
  • Ability to follow identity verification and access control procedures.
  • Ability to work independently while collaborating with a remote team.
  • Strong accountability for assigned tasks and customer follow-up.
  • Ability to learn new software tools and adapt to workflow changes.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical colleagues.
  • Willingness to follow established support standards and escalation guidelines.
  • Availability to collaborate during required U.S. Eastern Time working hours.
  • Comfortable working in a growing software environment with evolving processes.

Nice to Have

  • Experience in a patient support or patient services role.
  • Experience working with healthcare technology or telehealth platforms.
  • Experience providing non-clinical support to patients.
  • Familiarity with patient intake and online questionnaire workflows.
  • Experience troubleshooting web-based account access issues.

  • Experience documenting technical problems for engineering teams.
  • Familiarity with healthcare privacy and security practices.
  • Experience following identity verification procedures.
  • Experience maintaining internal support documentation or knowledge bases.
  • Experience identifying recurring support issues and reporting trends.
  • Experience supporting SaaS platforms or web-based applications.
  • Familiarity with e-commerce storefronts and online payment workflows.

  • Experience collaborating with technical support teams.
  • Experience working remotely with distributed teams.
  • Experience coordinating administrative requests with healthcare or pharmacy operations teams.

jobs.title: Video Editor and Video Creator
jobs.description:
About Measure Marketing

Measure Marketing is a performance-driven marketing agency specializing in demand generation, inbound marketing, and full-funnel strategies that help B2B companies turn data into measurable growth. Our team combines strategy, creativity, and analytics to deliver impactful digital marketing for a diverse client base, producing compelling content and campaigns that engage audiences and drive real business results. We are a dynamic, collaborative team seeking a talented Video Editor who can adapt to multiple brand voices and produce high-quality video content that supports our clients’ marketing and growth objectives.

Position Overview

We are looking for a skilled Video Editor with a minimum of 3 years of professional experience to join our marketing agency’s content team. In this role, you will edit and produce video content for multiple clients across different industries, requiring a strong ability to adapt to different brand voices, visual styles, and campaign objectives.

The ideal candidate understands the nuances of short-form, social-first content as well as long-form video, and can efficiently manage multiple projects while maintaining high creative and production standards.

Key Responsibilities

Video Editing & Production

  • Edit and produce engaging video content for multiple client brands across platforms including social media, YouTube, websites, and digital campaigns.
  • Create and edit short-form content (Reels, Shorts) as well as long-form videos and YouTube contentaligned with each client’s marketing strategy.
  • Adapt editing styles to match different brand voices, visual identities, and audience expectations.
  • Optimize video formats, pacing, captions, transitions, and structure for platform-specific performance and audience engagement.
  • Manage multiple client video projects simultaneously, meeting deadlines while maintaining high production quality.
  • Incorporate internal team and client feedback efficiently to refine and finalize video deliverables.
  • Maintain organized video asset libraries, project files, and templates to streamline workflows across multiple accounts.

Content Creation & Strategy

  • Contribute to the planning, development, and execution of strategic content across platforms including LinkedIn, Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and YouTube.
  • Craft and edit compelling, brand-aligned visual storytelling that supports broader marketing and SEO objectives with Social Media Specilist.
  • Collaborate with strategists, designers, and content marketers to develop video concepts, scripts, storyboards, and campaign content.
  • Ensure content supports inbound marketing campaigns and cross-channel brand consistency.

Visual Design & Creative Execution

  • Produce visually engaging digital content including branded videos, motion graphics, reels, and social media assets.
  • Apply client brand guidelines consistently while innovating with new formats and creative approaches.
  • Leverage motion graphics, animations, and visual storytelling techniques to increase engagement and content performance.

Innovation & Workflow Management

  • Stay ahead of emerging trends, editing techniques, AI tools, and platform algorithm changes to keep client content competitive.
  • Assist in managing publishing workflows and asset delivery across content management or scheduling platforms.
  • Continuously refine editing workflows and templates to increase production efficiency and scalability across accounts.

Data-Driven Optimization

  • Monitor video and content performance metrics such as engagement, reach, retention, and conversions.
  • Support the development of content insights and recommendations based on analytics.
  • Use performance data to test, refine, and scale high-performing video formats and storytelling approaches.

Skills and Qualifications

  • 3+ years of professional video editing experience, ideally within a marketing agency, media company, or content production environment.
  • Proficiency in Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, and Adobe Creative Suite.
  • Experience using AI-powered editing tools and automation workflows to improve efficiency and scale content production.
  • Strong understanding of storytelling, pacing, transitions, motion design, and visual engagement techniques.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, clients, and deadlines simultaneously in a fast-paced environment.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration skills when working with internal teams and clients.
  • Creative mindset with a strong eye for detail, visual consistency, and brand alignment.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience working in a marketing agency or multi-client environment.
  • Skills in motion graphics, animation, and visual effects.
  • Familiarity with video SEO, YouTube optimization, and social platform best practices.
  • Experience creating performance-focused content designed to drive engagement, leads, or conversions.

Why Join Measure Marketing?

We offer a competitive salary and benefits package along with a flexible remote working environment where your creativity and ideas are valued. You’ll work with a passionate, collaborative team and gain exposure to a wide range of industries and campaign types. We support continuous learning, certifications, and professional development, providing opportunities to grow your skills while contributing to meaningful, data-driven marketing that combines performance, strategy, and creativity.

About Bask Health

Bask Health is a software platform that enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses.

Our platform brings together patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Our teams work closely across product, engineering, customer success, sales, and company leadership to bring new capabilities to market and continuously improve the platform.

At Bask, product marketing plays an important role in connecting what we build with the businesses that use it. We value clear communication, a strong understanding of our customers, and the ability to turn complex product capabilities into practical value.

About the Role

We're looking for a Product Marketing Manager, Merchant Platform & Growth to help develop product positioning, execute go-to-market initiatives, and drive awareness and adoption of Bask Health's merchant-facing software capabilities.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform connects patient experiences, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce tools in one place.

As a Product Marketing Manager, you'll help communicate the value of Bask Health's merchant platform to prospective and existing customers.

You'll work closely with product managers, engineers, sales, customer success, growth marketing, and company leadership to translate product capabilities into clear messaging and customer-facing materials.

This role requires someone who understands B2B SaaS products and can explain how software helps entrepreneurs launch, operate, and grow their businesses.

You'll develop messaging for merchant-facing capabilities, including storefront configuration, product catalogs, subscriptions, checkout experiences, and business management tools.

You'll help customers understand how these capabilities fit together and how they support the day-to-day operation of a telehealth business.

You'll work with product teams to understand upcoming features and identify the customer problems they solve.

You'll help coordinate product launches, develop launch materials, and ensure internal teams have the information they need to communicate new capabilities.

A major part of this role will involve creating practical product marketing content that makes complex software easier for customers to understand.

You'll develop feature overviews, product presentations, sales enablement resources, customer education materials, and website messaging.

You'll partner with sales teams to understand common customer questions, objections, and competitive comparisons.

You'll use that feedback to improve messaging and create materials that support more effective product conversations.

You'll conduct customer research to better understand merchant needs, purchasing motivations, onboarding challenges, and product usage patterns.

You'll help analyze how product messaging and launches influence customer acquisition, activation, and adoption.

You'll collaborate with growth marketing stakeholders on campaigns that introduce relevant platform capabilities to prospective customers.

You'll also monitor competing e-commerce SaaS and merchant enablement platforms to identify useful market insights.

jobs.title: Google Ads Media Buyer / Growth Strategist
jobs.description:
Everyone can run a search campaign. Almost nobody can tell you whether it worked.

That is the whole job.

Google will happily show you a 6x ROAS built almost entirely out of people who already knew your client's name. It will auto apply assets you did not ask for. It will report a number that makes a client feel great and tells you nothing about whether you grew the business.

So we do not hire people to manage Google Ads. We hire marketers who can tell the difference between demand they created and demand they harvested, and who can prove it to a client's face.

At Sweat Pants Agency we work with around 50 DTC and eCommerce brands, 20 to 25 of them on paid media. We spend $6 to $9M a month on Meta and $1 to $2M a month on Google. We are the only agency behind two INC #1 fastest growing brands, both from zero.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

We're an entrepreneurial, product-focused engineering team that values ownership, technical excellence, and building software that solves real problems. Engineers work closely with product teams and company leadership, take features from idea to production, and have a direct role in shaping the platform.

Engineering at Bask is AI-first and builder-led. We use tools like Cursor and Claude Code throughout development while maintaining high standards for reliability, testing, and software quality.

About the Role

We're looking for a Content Designer, Merchant Platform to help create clear, intuitive, and consistent content across Bask Health's merchant-facing software experiences.

Bask Health enables entrepreneurs, doctors, and healthcare businesses to launch, manage, and grow direct-to-consumer telehealth businesses. Our platform brings together storefront management, patient questionnaires, clinical workflows, pharmacy operations, and commerce capabilities.

As a Content Designer, Merchant Platform, you'll help business owners and their teams understand how to configure, operate, and manage their telehealth businesses through our software.

This is a hands-on product content role combining UX writing, content design, information architecture, and cross-functional collaboration.

You'll work on the language and information structures merchants encounter while setting up their accounts, configuring storefronts, managing products, navigating dashboards, and completing administrative tasks.

Merchant-facing software often includes complex settings, dependencies, and workflows. Your responsibility will be to make these experiences easier to understand without oversimplifying important functionality.

You'll write interface content such as navigation labels, setup instructions, helper text, tooltips, error messages, empty states, confirmations, and system notifications.

You'll also help organize information so merchants can understand which actions are available, what each setting controls, and how changes may affect their business operations.

A major focus of this position will be merchant onboarding and configuration. You'll help create clear guidance for users who may be launching a telehealth business for the first time, while also supporting experienced operators who need efficient access to advanced tools.

You'll collaborate closely with product designers to develop content alongside interface layouts, interaction patterns, and workflow structures.

You'll work with product managers to understand merchant needs, business requirements, and product functionality.

You'll also partner with engineers to ensure content is implemented accurately, particularly in interfaces involving conditional settings, validation rules, and dynamically generated messages.

You'll collaborate with Customer Success and support teams to identify recurring merchant questions, confusing terminology, and areas where better in-product guidance could reduce unnecessary friction.

Because Bask supports healthcare-related businesses, you'll need to distinguish between merchant configuration responsibilities and clinical or pharmacy processes. You'll work with appropriate stakeholders to ensure specialized terminology and workflow descriptions are accurate.

You'll contribute to consistent terminology and reusable content patterns across the platform, helping merchants develop a clear understanding of Bask's tools as their businesses grow.

You'll use merchant feedback, usability research, and available product data to identify opportunities to improve comprehension, task completion, and the overall experience.

  • Apply plain-language and accessibility principles to business software interfaces.

You would own a set of our Google accounts end to end.

Here is what "end to end" actually means.

You are the account manager. We do not have any. You talk to the client directly. You write the updates, you run the calls, and you defend the call you made. The reason we do it this way is ownership. When you are the person answering for the account, it is your result, not somebody else's summary of your result.

You own the whole funnel, not the campaign. Feed and Merchant Center, search and Shopping and PMax, Demand Gen and YouTube, the landing page, and the conversion tracking underneath all of it. If the feed is why Shopping is starving, that is yours. If the page is why the clicks do not convert, that is yours too. Our team ships advertorials, comparison pages, and PDPs in Claude Code, deploys them to Vercel, points a subdomain at them, and tests them live before anything touches the client's Shopify theme.

You are expected to have an opinion about attribution and to defend it. We optimize to NC-CPA and NC-ROAS, not blended and not last click. We have turned brand search off to see what actually shifts to organic. We run geo holdouts. If a campaign is not incremental, we would rather know than keep the number.

You can live anywhere. We are remote and we hire worldwide. The one hard requirement is that you can take client calls during US Eastern business hours, because you are the client's point of contact. The rest of your day is yours. Nobody here is on a time clock. We judge you on output.

If you want a lane, a ticket queue, and a scope document, this is a bad fit and we will both know it fast.

If you want to own the whole picture and be judged on whether the number moved, keep reading.

Requirements

What the job looks like

  • Own a set of DTC accounts as the strategist, the buyer, and the client's direct point of contact. Budgets run from $5k/mo to well into six figures a month.
  • Own the client relationship. There is no account manager between you and them. You present the results, the plan, and the reasoning, and you are the one who answers when something is not working.
  • Audit before you touch anything. Every account we take over gets a real review first: campaign and ad group structure, keywords versus search terms, negatives, bidding strategy per campaign type, impression share, feed health, landing pages, audiences, and conversion tracking. Then a Loom walking the client through what you found. That Loom is how we sell and it is how we keep people.
  • Run brand and non brand as different businesses. Brand is mostly assisted conversion and it usually belongs on target impression share, not target CPA. Non brand is where the growth is and where the waste is. Report them separately or you are reporting nothing.
  • Know what PMax is actually doing. The most common mistake we see is optimizing PMax against an incremental CAC when half the volume inside it is branded. If you cannot separate those two, you cannot set a target.
  • Keep Google's automation on a leash. Auto applied recommendations, auto applied assets, and auto created sitelinks have cost our clients real money. We audit for them on a schedule.
  • Own the feed. Merchant Center hygiene, product titles, disapprovals, promotions, and what the feed does to Shopping and PMax delivery.
  • Own the tracking. GA4, GTM, Shopify goal imports versus a raw Google Ads tag, enhanced conversions, offline conversion imports for the lead gen accounts. When the numbers do not reconcile, you are the one who finds out why.
  • Diagnose the bottleneck, then go fix it. Creative, offer, AOV, landing page, checkout, tracking. Nobody is going to reassign it to another team.
  • Build the things the account needs. Landing pages, scripts, reporting, whatever removes the constraint. We are heavy AI users and we expect you to build, not just prompt.

You are a fit if

  • You have done this with real money. Hands on Google Ads at meaningful spend on DTC and eCommerce, with results you can walk us through: CPA, ROAS, revenue, and what you actually changed to get them. Shopping and PMax specifically, not just search.
  • You are fluent in the whole stack, not one campaign type. Search, Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen, YouTube, Merchant Center, GA4, GTM. Bing is a nice to have.
  • You are AI native, and you build. This is a requirement, not a bonus. You should already be using Claude or equivalent as a working tool rather than a novelty, and you should be able to build and ship a landing page with it.
  • You can communicate your ideas in English at a native or near native level. You will be in front of clients constantly. You need to explain your thinking clearly, sell an idea on its merits, push back when a client is about to force the account into mediocrity, and raise a problem before it becomes a fire. This matters as much as anything else on this list.
  • You are skeptical of your own numbers. You would rather run the holdout than protect the dashboard.
  • You can work US Eastern business hours for client calls. Where you live is up to you.
  • Bonus: you have built or operated your own Shopify store, or you have run Meta at spend too.

You are not a fit if

  • "That was not my role" is in your vocabulary. It is the fastest way to end an interview here. If the feed was the problem on an account you ran, you should have done something about the feed.
  • You want to be told what to do this week.
  • You need a ticketing system to know what matters.
  • You quote blended ROAS as if it settles the question.

Benefits

Why this role is exciting

This is not a maintenance job. You would have real influence over how we run Google across the agency.

You will work on real brands with real budgets. We test aggressively. We learn quickly. We build frameworks that scale.

You get trust on day one. You get a lot of autonomy. Some people thrive with it. You will get feedback fast either way, and if you make it through the first 30 days you will probably be here for a long time. Our retention on this team is very good and that is not an accident.

You will grow into senior strategy. We want people who want more responsibility. If you perform, you will grow.

You’ll be a core part of our lift experimentation program, leading client lift tests from design through execution to final presentation.
